Hard to Be a God takes you through a world where people look directly into the camera and objects are constantly dangled in front of it, while faces and hands appear from nowhere like the lens is another person trying to make its way through each brutal scene. I absolutely love it and these are some Sunday morning ramblings as to why. The main character, Rumata, goes through a constant bombardment of requests and threats, alongside the filth and brutality of the society he is in. But for most of the film he takes almost everything in his stride, like he's super calm regardless of what mess is happening. He knows another kind of civilisation is possible and knows that something needs to change, but that doesn't mean he can do anything on his own. So he's kind of stuck in a perpetual cycle of guts and grime; back and forth with piss, snot and puddles and random machines and spikes and musical instruments and fog. But in spite of that, I never felt the film lacked 'progress' because I never really got why 'progress' needs to mean moving in a tidy way from one point to another. Life doesn't really work that way, or maybe it does for some folks, but it doesn't for social and technological development, despite how we might think that it does. Rumata basically continues living in this world where everything is interrupted and familiar problems return, with the Renaissance he knows could happen staying somewhere on the horizon beyond the moonshine, zits and donkey penises. The filthiness is probably pushed a bit too far, and 3 hours of hawking and traipsing through sludge, alongside lacerated butt cheeks and dead fish, totally becomes an endurance test - but that was also part of the fun. I didn't find it repetitive because the filmmaker finds so many different ways of presenting this world, particularly through the movement of the camera and the awesome use of props. It is disgusting and obscene, but it also has moments of despair and grief for characters whose lives I got interested in without necessarily identifying with them. The Baron, for instance, waving his sword around like a raging loon before ending up face down with arrows in his back was especially brutal. He had so much more to give! The film also left me thinking about a society where few people seem capable of imagining that things could be different, while Rumata knows that they can be and still can't work out how to make that change happen. His knowledge and his $$$ distinguishes him from the people around him, but he's not really superior cos he still spits and flings donkey poop, increasingly behaving like someone who belongs in that time and place. The thing that makes him different is that he knows another world is possible, while the film gradually tests how much that knowledge is worth when he can't create it himself. By the time he goes berserk and loses his restraint, the hours beforehand validate his spree, and I found the whole thing fascinating and totally unforgettable.

Civilization feels less like a promise than a distant illusion, swallowed by a world drowning in mud, cruelty, and endless decay. Every frame is suffocatingly alive, overflowing with bodies, filth, noise, and violence until history itself begins to resemble a nightmare without beginning or end. Rather than observing chaos from a safe distance, the film forces you to inhabit it, stripping away every trace of comfort as if humanity were trapped inside its own moral decomposition. Its greatness lies in the relentless conviction of its vision. Power, knowledge, and progress are rendered almost meaningless against the weight of ignorance and brutality, turning the story into something far larger than science fiction or historical allegory. It is an overwhelming meditation on the impossibility of redemption in a world unwilling to change, demanding endurance as much as attention. ★★★★★ — a monumental descent into the abyss of human barbarity, where history rots in plain sight and even gods are powerless before mankind.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews medianas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

A symphony of gimmicks and muddied waters. I hate to be that person again…. but I genuinely didn’t enjoy this at all. For me, possession/satanic cults and rituals as a trope usually lead to something, to some greater overarching plot. And although not everything needs to have a deeply moving message, this movie unfortunately feels like it lost its own in the process. A lot of the more memorable and twisted scenes only work and have the impact they do because they leverage that early gravitas of the potential exploration of grief, lose of youth/bodily autonomy, familial cycles and traumas, etc. But this film never truly makes that turn around back to the point it initially latched onto and conveniently lets go for the sake of shock factor. I’ll totally be the person to give the actors their flowers, and some of the scenes would not have functioned as such great pieces of storytelling if it was not for the camerawork. But aesthetics and talents can only take you so far. I think this has consistently been my gripe with Ari Aster is he has such great ideas and his attention to detail is insane, but are his grandiose projects fleshed out to begin with? Honestly no. He relies on the conversation and pushing the limits of what horror can be, which I do frankly respect him for; but again this, like a lot of his other work let me go as easily as it grabbed me. And genuinely I’m left with 0 takeaway from this… maybe I’m the problem

The recent surge of a particular brand of arthouse horror, favoring tension- and character-building over blood-fueled gonzo insanity, has found at a home in A24 with the likes of The Witch, It Comes at Night, and even Yorgos Lanthimos’ recent features. Their latest in the genre comes with Hereditary, the directorial debut from writer-director Ari Aster, which–as the title suggests–is less haunted house horror and more about the terror tied with psychologically-taut familial relations. Not unlike Robert Eggers’ Sundance sensation, Aster displays proficient skill in eerie tone-setting, elaborate production design, and the type of scares that will leave a pervasive imprint on the mind, even if the underlying mythology gets over-complicated by the finale. [16] nota=3.0 estrelas:
First of all, this film is not "this generation's 'The Exorcist.'" Nor is it "this generation's 'Rosemary's Baby'" for that matter. "Hereditary" doesn't come close to those classic horror films in terms of characterization or narrative coherence.  Toni Colette, Ann Dowd, and Alex Woolf all give very strong performances, and the film boasts some unusually creepy imagery, fabulous sound design (the doppler effect immerses us in the film, to the point that I swore I heard tongue clucking in the cab on the way home) and great sequences, rendering it a good, perhaps even very good, film. However, the story remains sketchy, and the ending in particular feels overwrought and unsatisfying, straining "suspension of disbelief."  There is not enough context for that resolution, as I saw it, so I felt stunned and a little let down. Which is really too bad, because the sequences leading up to it - directly after the "fire" scene - are extremely tense and quite frightening. The car scene with Peter and Charlie (I hope to see more of Milly Shapiro in future films!) is also brilliant & horrifying. It just doesn't come together **in terms of story.** Even the film's title is not clearly explained. There are intimations, but nothing is made clear. Don't get me wrong: ambiguity is fine; in fact, I usually love it. But "Hereditary" has too many loose threads to take it from very good to excellent. I will give it another watch, of course, to see if that changes for me. For now, I am glad I saw it in a theatre, and there is certainly lots to like, regardless of my critiques. I look forward to reading more reviews on here.

A symphony of gimmicks and muddied waters. I hate to be that person again…. but I genuinely didn’t enjoy this at all. For me, possession/satanic cults and rituals as a trope usually lead to something, to some greater overarching plot. And although not everything needs to have a deeply moving message, this movie unfortunately feels like it lost its own in the process. A lot of the more memorable and twisted scenes only work and have the impact they do because they leverage that early gravitas of the potential exploration of grief, lose of youth/bodily autonomy, familial cycles and traumas, etc. But this film never truly makes that turn around back to the point it initially latched onto and conveniently lets go for the sake of shock factor. I’ll totally be the person to give the actors their flowers, and some of the scenes would not have functioned as such great pieces of storytelling if it was not for the camerawork. But aesthetics and talents can only take you so far. I think this has consistently been my gripe with Ari Aster is he has such great ideas and his attention to detail is insane, but are his grandiose projects fleshed out to begin with? Honestly no. He relies on the conversation and pushing the limits of what horror can be, which I do frankly respect him for; but again this, like a lot of his other work let me go as easily as it grabbed me. And genuinely I’m left with 0 takeaway from this… maybe I’m the problem

[16] nota=3.0 estrelas:
First of all, this film is not "this generation's 'The Exorcist.'" Nor is it "this generation's 'Rosemary's Baby'" for that matter. "Hereditary" doesn't come close to those classic horror films in terms of characterization or narrative coherence.  Toni Colette, Ann Dowd, and Alex Woolf all give very strong performances, and the film boasts some unusually creepy imagery, fabulous sound design (the doppler effect immerses us in the film, to the point that I swore I heard tongue clucking in the cab on the way home) and great sequences, rendering it a good, perhaps even very good, film. However, the story remains sketchy, and the ending in particular feels overwrought and unsatisfying, straining "suspension of disbelief."  There is not enough context for that resolution, as I saw it, so I felt stunned and a little let down. Which is really too bad, because the sequences leading up to it - directly after the "fire" scene - are extremely tense and quite frightening. The car scene with Peter and Charlie (I hope to see more of Milly Shapiro in future films!) is also brilliant & horrifying. It just doesn't come together **in terms of story.** Even the film's title is not clearly explained. There are intimations, but nothing is made clear. Don't get me wrong: ambiguity is fine; in fact, I usually love it. But "Hereditary" has too many loose threads to take it from very good to excellent. I will give it another watch, of course, to see if that changes for me. For now, I am glad I saw it in a theatre, and there is certainly lots to like, regardless of my critiques. I look forward to reading more reviews on here.

About 6 months ago,  the world started seeing advertisements for a film that was touted as “a game changer” and “the scariest movie ever made”. People, myself included, started looking forward to the release of Hereditary. Recently, Letterboxd started filling with reviews for this much anticipated film - the most positive, enticing reviews I’ve seen. People I follow and trust gave 5 stars, a heart, and glowing reviews about holding back tears, almost passing out, being haunted by horrifying images. Tonight I finally saw this film that held so much promise and excitement. Two hours and change later, I’m absolutely shocked to find out that the past six months of hype and pointed, targeted advertising, along with the thousands of epic reviews on this site were actually all part of a very elaborate plot to punk me. It’s hard not to believe that this was all a Truman Show-esque experiment because otherwise that would mean that I really am this profoundly and inexcusably removed from the common consensus on what is good versus what is very, very bad. I’m sad and disillusioned. If this is the “future of modern horror” then I don’t think I can be a horror fan anymore. Boo

I spent thirty minutes after seeing the film to piece together everything, figured out all the clues, then realized I spent more time making the movie make sense than its director had. That said, the film is gorgeously shot, Toni Collette gives one of her most passionate performances and there are a couple of really creepy moments (which are completely undermined by the end of the film). It's the Michael Bay equivalent of a horror film, and about as incongruous as The Snowman, but gets by on shocking horror, and slick art direction. Hereditary is a narratively hollow culmination of ideas Ari Aster wrote on many napkins over a decade, stashed in a shoebox, then pulled out and scattered down a staircase to make a script. It bounces around various genres, concepts, plots, and themes, then haphazardly staples them together with elements of Rosemary's Baby. What it does well is evoke inventively disturbing imagery, underscored by immense dread. But then it takes all of it, and tries to stick it to its characters as well as sticking a slice of aloe to Teflon covered in motor oil. Its paper thin plot waffles between nebulous and overly expository. The characters are all one note, and underdeveloped. Whether it's Toni Collette who is crying or freaking out (nothing in between), Gabriel Byrne who's so skeptical, he doesn't even believe he's in the same movie, or Alex Wolff who plays a seventeen year old, but cries like a four year old. This is being treated as the second coming of The Exorcist (or insert whichever movie was seen as the scariest for its time). But it seems to really just be getting far off of its hype.

It is easy to figure out what exactly is going on and the scariest thing is that it'll confirm your own presumptions that this film has nowhere new to go. In fact, it lamely falls back on the kind of final half hour that dissolves first, into absurdity, and second, into cynicism. What does that leave us with? A technical exercise and nothing more. What the film had set up was perfectly fine, and hilariously, its playing off well worn tropes of the horror genre by sheer force of will. But what the film fucks up, is that horror in one way or another, has to have more than just a bunch of creepy happenings and then the most routine, lame, and tired explanation to all those creepy happenings. Why does the director rely on dollhouses? Because the shots look cool. Why mine mental illness? Who cares. The big bad in this feels like a cheat. One in which I didn't have a single care or devotion to. And the film leaves it at that, which is so frustrating. The best kind of horror films leave us by confirming that our fears and emotions are justified, even if they are strongly ambiguous. What Hereditary does is try to explain why we should be afraid or why we were afraid before. It doesn't add up and it doesn't have the heart, nerve, or audacity to accept that. It would rather seem ambiguous and deep, as if it were pulling one over the audience, but its last trick is predictable, lazy, old news.

I wish I could like Hereditary more. It attempts to tap into a fear not engaged with enough: that is, hereditable disease/mental illness. Formerly, such diseases were incorporated into horror in a mystical or religious way, birth defects being a prime example. Such defects were alternatively viewed as divine or a curse, either being an elevation from normal existence. Now (by that I mean at least since the modern synthesis), with the scientific comphrension of herediability, a new sort of horror has arose. The horror of potentially damning your offspring to a life of suffering, though by no personal fault of your own. In this film, some scenes capture this anxity brilliantly, both from the mom and her son's perspective. Unfortunately, these scenes are invariably undermined by less-than-great acting or by being retroactively neutured (e.g. made into a dream). Even if the individual scene was allowed to breath (rarely), the overarching themes (doll-house, A24 etc), which weren't pulled together well, hampered the cinematography. I did like that the family (namely the father) was supportive, the "curse" of disease can strike anyone. The ending was also provocative (especially when read through the lens of mental illness). Also, maybe its just me (or that I had this movie partially spoiled), but it really wasn't that scary! Probably because it felt so pastiche?

Aims for a home run, but strikes out before it can get past the first act. Man, this was a major disappointment. It’s clear Aster has watched indie horror films of late (hence what probably caught A24’s attention) and late 60s/70s classics. Yet unlike It Follows, The Babadook & The Witch, Hereditary lacks a desire to establish pathos that engages its themes, which are so haphazardly spelled out in every scene instead of letting them develop organically between characters. This will fall prey to the “scary” hype, but as we’ve seen recently, good horror doesn’t have to be traditionally scary — or “scary” by what 15-year olds want. Collette is fine, but hysteria — for me — doesn’t always make a performance stand out for the right reasons. Wolff is, at times, unwatchable. Shapiro is the real star. As Collette’s Annie says, “And what a waste.”

[20] nota=2.0 estrelas:
The marketing's already begun and I'll admit I want to see it again. We heard whispers most of the festival about A24's hot new horror film, hearing many people say what's now in the marketing, that Hereditary is the new scariest film ever. While having that air of new horror I've written about before, Hereditary lacks the compelling story that truly would have had this grind my insides. This does a ton correctly that I'll praise. It builds up the tension immensely well, traversing at a deliberate pace that ramps up the dread perfectly. Something creepy looms on the horizon for a long time, daring the viewer that it will appear at any moment. But as a horror film going over two hours, that sense of loom ultimately gets to be too much. Hereditary doesn't give a release. It builds and builds, promising an explanation to the madness unfolding on screen only to drag on too long and not give any satisfactory answers. While effective in its horror, as the film gets to the truly terrifying moments, I had already lost faith that it would have any meaning. Hereditary does enough right to not be considered bad, but its also unbelievably frustrating in its attempts to mask the lack of a story with horror. Overall, I'll likely still see it again just to have a second opinion, yet I won't likely be able to forgive the problems riddling the film just because it builds the horror correctly.

[21] nota=2.0 estrelas:
It's the Michael Bay equivalent of a horror film, and about as incongruous as The Snowman, but gets by on shocking horror, and slick art direction. Hereditary is a narratively hollow culmination of ideas Ari Aster wrote on many napkins over a decade, stashed in a shoebox, then pulled out and scattered down a staircase to make a script. It bounces around various genres, concepts, plots, and themes, then haphazardly staples them together with elements of Rosemary's Baby. What it does well is evoke inventively disturbing imagery, underscored by immense dread. But then it takes all of it, and tries to stick it to its characters as well as sticking a slice of aloe to Teflon covered in motor oil. Its paper thin plot waffles between nebulous and overly expository. The characters are all one note, and underdeveloped. Whether it's Toni Collette who is crying or freaking out (nothing in between), Gabriel Byrne who's so skeptical, he doesn't even believe he's in the same movie, or Alex Wolff who plays a seventeen year old, but cries like a four year old. This is being treated as the second coming of The Exorcist (or insert whichever movie was seen as the scariest for its time). But it seems to really just be getting far off of its hype.

[23] nota=2.0 estrelas:
Okay A24--we're done. No more of these half-realized genre pics, technical exercise, calling cards. May Under The Skin remain the only great film you've released(okay and Spring Breakers). So what's wrong with Hereditary ? It's cynical but not so obviously at first. The first half begins with quite an unexpected plot point and builds upon it with an eerie, grief felt, and almost at the edge of tears/laughter kind of atmosphere. It is refreshing that the film doesn't cheaply go for jump scares(make of that whatever you will) and god damn, Toni Collette is great. She's perfect for this kind of role, too bad it's stuck in a movie that in turn, leads her character into one of the most tired resolutions. And really, that's where this film comes undone. It is easy to figure out what exactly is going on and the scariest thing is that it'll confirm your own presumptions that this film has nowhere new to go. In fact, it lamely falls back on the kind of final half hour that dissolves first, into absurdity, and second, into cynicism. What does that leave us with? A technical exercise and nothing more. What the film had set up was perfectly fine, and hilariously, its playing off well worn tropes of the horror genre by sheer force of will. But what the film fucks up, is that horror in one way or another, has to have more than just a bunch of creepy happenings and then the most routine, lame, and tired explanation to all those creepy happenings. Why does the director rely on dollhouses? Because the shots look cool. Why mine mental illness? Who cares. The big bad in this feels like a cheat. One in which I didn't have a single care or devotion to. And the film leaves it at that, which is so frustrating. The best kind of horror films leave us by confirming that our fears and emotions are justified, even if they are strongly ambiguous. What Hereditary does is try to explain why we should be afraid or why we were afraid before. It doesn't add up and it doesn't have the heart, nerve, or audacity to accept that. It would rather seem ambiguous and deep, as if it were pulling one over the audience, but its last trick is predictable, lazy, old news.

I wish I could like Hereditary more. It attempts to tap into a fear not engaged with enough: that is, hereditable disease/mental illness. Formerly, such diseases were incorporated into horror in a mystical or religious way, birth defects being a prime example. Such defects were alternatively viewed as divine or a curse, either being an elevation from normal existence. Now (by that I mean at least since the modern synthesis), with the scientific comphrension of herediability, a new sort of horror has arose. The horror of potentially damning your offspring to a life of suffering, though by no personal fault of your own. In this film, some scenes capture this anxity brilliantly, both from the mom and her son's perspective. Unfortunately, these scenes are invariably undermined by less-than-great acting or by being retroactively neutured (e.g. made into a dream). Even if the individual scene was allowed to breath (rarely), the overarching themes (doll-house, A24 etc), which weren't pulled together well, hampered the cinematography. I did like that the family (namely the father) was supportive, the "curse" of disease can strike anyone. The ending was also provocative (especially when read through the lens of mental illness). Also, maybe its just me (or that I had this movie partially spoiled), but it really wasn't that scary! Probably because it felt so pastiche?

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "medianas" (2.5–3 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews medianas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Las actuaciones de los jóvenes actores son excelentes. Torres ofrece una actuación sutil y conmovedora en la que sus ojos transmiten más que mil palabras. Delgada y elegante. Es un fuerte recordatorio de los peligros de que los gobiernos tengan demasiado poder y de por qué es tan importante proteger la democracia. I'm Still Here es un drama histórico sólido sobre la dictadura militar brasileña, pero creo que exige una conexión emocional con ese contexto que, al menos en mi caso, nunca terminó de aparecer. Entiendo perfectamente la importancia que tiene para Brasil recuperar esta historia y poner rostro a las víctimas de un régimen que persiguió, secuestró e hizo desaparecer a quienes consideraba una amenaza. Precisamente por eso se entiende el enorme reconocimiento que ha recibido: ganó el Óscar a la Mejor Película Internacional y el Goya a la Mejor Película Iberoamericana. La película funciona muy bien mostrando la lucha institucional de Eunice Paiva por mantener viva la memoria de su marido frente a un Estado que pretende borrar cualquier rastro de sus crímenes. Es un relato sobre la burocracia, la resistencia y la dignidad mucho más que sobre la violencia explícita de la dictadura. Sin embargo, no terminé de conectar con ella. El ritmo es muy pausado, la historia avanza lentamente y la sensación de impotencia acaba pesando más que el propio conflicto. Entiendo que esa sea precisamente la intención del director, pero personalmente esperaba una propuesta con un desarrollo más intenso o un conflicto narrativo que me atrapara más. No me parece una mala película; al contrario, está muy bien hecha y comprendo perfectamente su relevancia histórica y política. Simplemente creo que pertenece a esa categoría de películas impecables en su ejecución, pero que difícilmente recordaré dentro de unos años. Para mí se queda en un 3/5: buena, necesaria y respetable, pero sin llegar a emocionarme tanto como esperaba.

ای! فیلم با جهان خانواده و با محوریت شخصیت اصلی یعنی (مادر خانه) آغاز میشود، جهانی که گه گاه اشاراتی به فضای سیاسی جامعه برزیل دارد اما تکیه بر خانواده ای و پرجمعیت که احتمالا قرار است اتفاقی باعث از هم پاشیدگی یا اسیب به ان میشود. اتفاقا نقطه عطف داستان یعنی گرفتار شدن روبنس سبب میشود که کارگردان به دلیل عدم انتخاب در زاویه نسبت به روایت خود باعث میگردد که روایت بلاتکلیف بماند و خانواداه ای که در به طبع آن اونیسی و دخترشان اندکی فضای فیلم که نگاه سیاسی در آن غالب است سعی دارد آن رعب و وحشت و بی‌منطقی حاکم را بسازد اما در آن موفق نیست. بعد از این است که روایت دچار افت معنا و فرم میشود و شخصیت‌های سرگردان (به خصوص فرعی مانند وکیل یا روزنامه‌نگاران و دوستان روبنس) باعث میگردد که اثرات سنگینی که میتواند چنین اتفاقی بر خانواده بگذارد مشاهده ننماییم. در نهایت روایت داستان در جایی که خانواده تصمیم به ترک و رفتن به سائوپائولو میگیرند پایان میپذیرد که همین نقطه نیز توانایی ساخت یک روایت تمام کمال را ندارد اما از نظر پایان بندی میتوانست نقطه مناسبی باشد. اما به دلیل وفادار بودن ماجرا را متحمل است، بلکه برای اینکه نامه گواهی فوت روبنس به دست اونیسی برسد و در فیلم ثبت گردد. عجیبتر اینکه باز هم 18 سال پیش میرویم و یک خانواده را میبینیم که هیچ بازتاب دراماتیک ندارند و تنها برای اینکه ما ناگهان اونیسی را در حال دیدن گزارشی از قهرمان بودن روبنس ببیند. این مخ آخر به این روایت ناقص و ضعیف است. البته نمی‌توان از سکانس‌های خوبی در ابتدای فیلم که مربوط به خانواده است صرفه نظر کرد، هرچند که نمی‌توان به فرزندان نزدیک شد به این دلیل که فیلم بیش از حد متکی به شخصیت اصلی (اونیسی) است و همان را هم ناقص می‌سازد. همچنین بازی خوب .. در نقش اونیسی نیز باعث شده که فیلم تحمل‌پذیرتر باشد. در مجموع روایتی ناقص و بی‌هدف که تکلیفش با خودش مشخص نیست، باعث می‌شود فیلم به یک فیلم متوسط تنزل پیدا کند.

Dieser Film hat mich an manchen Stellen tief berührt. Doch mein Rating variiert zu verschiedenen Zeitpunkten stark. Die Hauptdarstellerin und die Figur der Mutter sind für mich das Schönste gewesen - man sieht sie nicht in Selbstmitleid verfallen, sie ist unerschütterlich tapfer, radikal pragmatisch, strahlt Besonnenheit aus und dann diese rührende Zärtlichkeit ihrer Familie gegenüber - und zeitgleich sieht man ihr an, wie sie der Verlust des Mannes und dessen Umstände unwiderruflich gebrochen haben. Sie strahlt zum einen leise Hoffnung, Resilienz, aber zum anderen endlose Melancholie aus. Dieses Schauspiel verdient wirklich Aufmerksamkeit, Fernanda Torres ist unglaublich charismatisch. Zum Ende des zweiten Akts möchte ich dem Film somit gern vier Sterne geben. Aber in anderen Momenten verfällt der Film in Kitsch, wie im letzten Akt - das ist wirklich ärgerlich. Außerdem kratzt mir der Film zu sehr an der Oberfläche, ist unpolitisch und fokussiert sich zu sehr auf die Biografie des Einzelnen. Da würde ich doch am liebsten nur 2 1/2 Sterne geben aus reinem Trotz. So fühlt sich mein Fazit nicht ganz authentisch an. Dem hohem Averagerating kann ich mich nicht anschließen, für ein Meisterwerk halte ich den Film bei Weitem nicht. Da er trotz Laufzeit erstaunlich kurzweilig und unanstrengend ist, bin ich milde gestimmt.

I'm Still Here es un drama histórico sólido sobre la dictadura militar brasileña, pero creo que exige una conexión emocional con ese contexto que, al menos en mi caso, nunca terminó de aparecer. Entiendo perfectamente la importancia que tiene para Brasil recuperar esta historia y poner rostro a las víctimas de un régimen que persiguió, secuestró e hizo desaparecer a quienes consideraba una amenaza. Precisamente por eso se entiende el enorme reconocimiento que ha recibido: ganó el Óscar a la Mejor Película Internacional y el Goya a la Mejor Película Iberoamericana. La película funciona muy bien mostrando la lucha institucional de Eunice Paiva por mantener viva la memoria de su marido frente a un Estado que pretende borrar cualquier rastro de sus crímenes. Es un relato sobre la burocracia, la resistencia y la dignidad mucho más que sobre la violencia explícita de la dictadura. Sin embargo, no terminé de conectar con ella. El ritmo es muy pausado, la historia avanza lentamente y la sensación de impotencia acaba pesando más que el propio conflicto. Entiendo que esa sea precisamente la intención del director, pero personalmente esperaba una propuesta con un desarrollo más intenso o un conflicto narrativo que me atrapara más. No me parece una mala película; al contrario, está muy bien hecha y comprendo perfectamente su relevancia histórica y política. Simplemente creo que pertenece a esa categoría de películas impecables en su ejecución, pero que difícilmente recordaré dentro de unos años. Para mí se queda en un 3/5: buena, necesaria y respetable, pero sin llegar a emocionarme tanto como esperaba.

[1] nota=0.5 estrelas:
Este filme representa, a meu ver, tudo aquilo que há de mais problemático no cinema nacional contemporâneo. É um insulto à tradição artística construída por cineastas que buscaram desenvolver uma linguagem verdadeiramente brasileira para a sétima arte. Saímos da ambição estética e intelectual de Glauber Rocha, responsável por obras fundamentais como Terra em Transe e Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol, passamos por realizadores como Nelson Pereira dos Santos e José Mojica Marins, que ajudaram a consolidar uma identidade própria para o cinema brasileiro, para chegarmos a produções como esta, inteiramente subordinadas à lógica do melodrama televisivo e da padronização estética importada do audiovisual norte-americano. O filme permanece preso ao nível mais superficial de apreensão estética. Qualquer sensação de profundidade surge menos de sua construção narrativa do que de expedientes psicológicos cuidadosamente calculados para provocar respostas afetivas automáticas. Tudo parece subordinado à lógica mercadológica: a identidade nacional, a riqueza cultural brasileira e a complexidade dramática são sacrificadas em favor da acessibilidade imediata e da rentabilidade, é o exemplo máximo do Brasil descartando seu cinema como arte para transforma-lo em mero produto e propagando fazendo uma representação porca de sua própria realidade, com um diretor de fotografia sem criatividade e atores que acham que estão em uma novela da globo.

Itaú. Um banco que, durante a ditadura militar brasileira, beneficiou-se de políticas econômicas que favoreciam a concentração bancária e o crescimento de instituições privadas, expandindo significativamente durante o regime por meio de fusões e aquisições incentivadas pelos governos militares. Walter Moreira Salles Júnior, herdeiro neoliberal bilionário do Itaú, decidiu fazer um filme retratando os horrores causados pela ditadura militar. Me sinto repetindo a exata mesma crítica que fiz em "Barbie". Aqui nós temos mais um filme cínico feito da burguesia para a burguesia, onde a trama é centrada em uma família de classe média alta no Rio de Janeiro. Essa escolha possui seus méritos, a dor da família Paiva é real, profunda e incontestável, mas esse recorte social estreito não representa a complexidade do trauma coletivo causado pelo regime militar. Algumas pessoas argumentam que "Esse é um filme sobre a família", mas esse filme sobre família está inserido em um contexto político de um momento extremamente grave na história brasileira, onde o filme não abre espaço para uma verdadeira discussão politica, para confrontar o que está sendo narrado, para denunciar os horrores da ditadura. Esse é um filme despolitizante que quer passar a impressão de ser um filme político. A empregada da família Paiva, que provavelmente vivia sob vigilância, com medo e em condições precarias (diferente da família Paiva, ela advém de uma classe social que não tinha voz, educação ou qualquer capital simbólico) recebe um tratamento decorativo apenas. Ignorar figuras como ela em um pais onde a ditadura aprofundou desigualdades raciais e de classe, não foi uma escolha dramática artística do diretor, foi apenas silêncio político intencional. Isso vale também para os guerrilheiros urbanos que são apenas um detalhe implícito no filme, onde o filme evita confrontar essas figuras e realizar um embate ideológico, privilegiando o luto privado. Aqui a ditadura é representada de forma muito vaga, parecendo muito mais uma força abstrata e cruel do que um projeto de poder enfrentado ativamente por diferentes figuras históricas. Aquele momento totalmente jogado do soldado do bem que diz "saiba que eu não concordo com isso" é quase cômico. Nada do que escrevi diminui ou menospreza o sofrimento da família Paiva, já que a repressão destruiu sua rotina familiar. Porém, ao tratar a ditadura militar de forma tão vaga e ignorando outros recortes sociais, o filme torna-se um drama comum. Por fim, o filme adota a linguagem clássica com começo bem definido, desenvolvimento da história com conclusão emocionante, arco dramático da protagonista, fotografia perfeitamente satisfatória, figurino perfeitamente satisfatório e direção perfeitamente satisfatória com cortes suaves e uma trilha sonora que induz emoção nos momentos escolhidos. A escolha pouco inspirada de conceber a obra aos moldes de Hollywood, de retratar uma história num contexto político grave (mas sem levantar uma discussão política real) somada com todo o cuidado técnico, transforma esse filme em um típico filme de padrão internacional feito para ganhar prêmios em festivais e na cerimônia política de autopromoção dos EUA. Me parece que o filme foi realizado única e exclusivamente nesse intuito... Bem, ele conseguiu. No entanto, de longe esse filme representa toda a diversidade e criatividade artística que o cinema brasileiro pode proporcionar. A torcida pesada que esse filme teve para ganhar o Oscar reflete como estamos culturalmente colonizados.

La folie et la douleur auxquelles les personnages devraient être sujets sont complètement reniées, tout est fait pour paraître plus doux (le gardien de prison qui est gentil mdrrr j’étais à deux doigts de couper le film). Apesar de ter muitos méritos, como a atuação poderosa de Fernanda Torres, a bela cinematografia que acompanha todo o filme, a dor de ver uma família destruída por um fato que durou 21 anos no Brasil e a demonstração de como era a perseguição a dissidentes e críticos àquele regime imposto, I'm Still Here erra ao tentar ser um filme e, ao mesmo tempo, uma novela das 9:00 horas produzida pela TV Globo. Isso deve-se principalmente à forma pela qual Walter dirige, monta, cria e coloca os diálogos, constrói a trama e aplica filtros de cores ao seu filme, que remontam diretamente aos modelos e convenções novelísticas moldados por décadas pelas principais emissoras nacionais e internacionais, como as falas explícitas sem a construção do silêncio, as explosões de emoção dos personagens -- o que os faz parecerem um pouco irreais -- e o uso excessivo de meios dramáticos fáceis demais. Uma cena que exemplifica isso é o momento em que as crianças vão ao escritório do pai para mostrar o novo cachorro, pois embora seja uma cena de felicidade das crianças e, consequentemente, de seu pai com o novo cachorro, ela se assemelha muito à construção de cena de dramaturgia, graças aos diálogos, à reação do pai e do colega e à cor pastel que reforçam essa sensação durante todo o longa. A principal explicação desse estranhamento que atravessa a obra tem raízes na forma como o Brasil constrói e construiu suas artes. Desde a popularização do cinema nacional no meio internacional, muitas produtoras e distribuidoras têm escolhido o que é mais fácil e melhor para elas no sentido econômico e cultural: a contratação de atores de novelas para filmes, já que são rostos conhecidos pelo público e têm uma bagagem de atuação muito maior que um ator que está dando seus primeiros passos. Por isso, mesmo nascendo puramente como um longa-metragem, sua raiz pivotal está presa e ligada às novelas, e I'm Still Here sofre com essa dicotomia. Portanto, um dos maiores problemas do cinema nacional é o fato de sempre conversar e ter em seu âmago as regras e padrões da teledramaturgia, não obstante seja uma obra feita para o cinema. Por esse motivo, I'm Still Here , ainda que trate de um assunto pesado e espinhoso que permeia a sociedade brasileira, sofre com crise de identidade, não sabendo se é um drama televisivo ou um longa-metragem -- embora tenha muitos méritos que poderiam atingir seu auge caso se desprendessem das convenções de um meio do qual não faz parte.

Itaú. Um banco que, durante a ditadura militar brasileira, beneficiou-se de políticas econômicas que favoreciam a concentração bancária e o crescimento de instituições privadas, expandindo significativamente durante o regime por meio de fusões e aquisições incentivadas pelos governos militares. Walter Moreira Salles Júnior, herdeiro neoliberal bilionário do Itaú, decidiu fazer um filme retratando os horrores causados pela ditadura militar. Me sinto repetindo a exata mesma crítica que fiz em "Barbie". Aqui nós temos mais um filme cínico feito da burguesia para a burguesia, onde a trama é centrada em uma família de classe média alta no Rio de Janeiro. Essa escolha possui seus méritos, a dor da família Paiva é real, profunda e incontestável, mas esse recorte social estreito não representa a complexidade do trauma coletivo causado pelo regime militar. Algumas pessoas argumentam que "Esse é um filme sobre a família", mas esse filme sobre família está inserido em um contexto político de um momento extremamente grave na história brasileira, onde o filme não abre espaço para uma verdadeira discussão politica, para confrontar o que está sendo narrado, para denunciar os horrores da ditadura. Esse é um filme despolitizante que quer passar a impressão de ser um filme político. A empregada da família Paiva, que provavelmente vivia sob vigilância, com medo e em condições precarias (diferente da família Paiva, ela advém de uma classe social que não tinha voz, educação ou qualquer capital simbólico) recebe um tratamento decorativo apenas. Ignorar figuras como ela em um pais onde a ditadura aprofundou desigualdades raciais e de classe, não foi uma escolha dramática artística do diretor, foi apenas silêncio político intencional. Isso vale também para os guerrilheiros urbanos que são apenas um detalhe implícito no filme, onde o filme evita confrontar essas figuras e realizar um embate ideológico, privilegiando o luto privado. Aqui a ditadura é representada de forma muito vaga, parecendo muito mais uma força abstrata e cruel do que um projeto de poder enfrentado ativamente por diferentes figuras históricas. Aquele momento totalmente jogado do soldado do bem que diz "saiba que eu não concordo com isso" é quase cômico. Nada do que escrevi diminui ou menospreza o sofrimento da família Paiva, já que a repressão destruiu sua rotina familiar. Porém, ao tratar a ditadura militar de forma tão vaga e ignorando outros recortes sociais, o filme torna-se um drama comum. Por fim, o filme adota a linguagem clássica com começo bem definido, desenvolvimento da história com conclusão emocionante, arco dramático da protagonista, fotografia perfeitamente satisfatória, figurino perfeitamente satisfatório e direção perfeitamente satisfatória com cortes suaves e uma trilha sonora que induz emoção nos momentos escolhidos. A escolha pouco inspirada de conceber a obra aos moldes de Hollywood, de retratar uma história num contexto político grave (mas sem levantar uma discussão política real) somada com todo o cuidado técnico, transforma esse filme em um típico filme de padrão internacional feito para ganhar prêmios em festivais e na cerimônia política de autopromoção dos EUA. Me parece que o filme foi realizado única e exclusivamente nesse intuito... Bem, ele conseguiu. No entanto, de longe esse filme representa toda a diversidade e criatividade artística que o cinema brasileiro pode proporcionar. A torcida pesada que esse filme teve para ganhar o Oscar reflete como estamos culturalmente colonizados.

Apesar de ter muitos méritos, como a atuação poderosa de Fernanda Torres, a bela cinematografia que acompanha todo o filme, a dor de ver uma família destruída por um fato que durou 21 anos no Brasil e a demonstração de como era a perseguição a dissidentes e críticos àquele regime imposto, I'm Still Here erra ao tentar ser um filme e, ao mesmo tempo, uma novela das 9:00 horas produzida pela TV Globo. Isso deve-se principalmente à forma pela qual Walter dirige, monta, cria e coloca os diálogos, constrói a trama e aplica filtros de cores ao seu filme, que remontam diretamente aos modelos e convenções novelísticas moldados por décadas pelas principais emissoras nacionais e internacionais, como as falas explícitas sem a construção do silêncio, as explosões de emoção dos personagens -- o que os faz parecerem um pouco irreais -- e o uso excessivo de meios dramáticos fáceis demais. Uma cena que exemplifica isso é o momento em que as crianças vão ao escritório do pai para mostrar o novo cachorro, pois embora seja uma cena de felicidade das crianças e, consequentemente, de seu pai com o novo cachorro, ela se assemelha muito à construção de cena de dramaturgia, graças aos diálogos, à reação do pai e do colega e à cor pastel que reforçam essa sensação durante todo o longa. A principal explicação desse estranhamento que atravessa a obra tem raízes na forma como o Brasil constrói e construiu suas artes. Desde a popularização do cinema nacional no meio internacional, muitas produtoras e distribuidoras têm escolhido o que é mais fácil e melhor para elas no sentido econômico e cultural: a contratação de atores de novelas para filmes, já que são rostos conhecidos pelo público e têm uma bagagem de atuação muito maior que um ator que está dando seus primeiros passos. Por isso, mesmo nascendo puramente como um longa-metragem, sua raiz pivotal está presa e ligada às novelas, e I'm Still Here sofre com essa dicotomia. Portanto, um dos maiores problemas do cinema nacional é o fato de sempre conversar e ter em seu âmago as regras e padrões da teledramaturgia, não obstante seja uma obra feita para o cinema. Por esse motivo, I'm Still Here , ainda que trate de um assunto pesado e espinhoso que permeia a sociedade brasileira, sofre com crise de identidade, não sabendo se é um drama televisivo ou um longa-metragem -- embora tenha muitos méritos que poderiam atingir seu auge caso se desprendessem das convenções de um meio do qual não faz parte.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.

3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.

Very gripping true story! Very sickening too if I’m honest - dictatorships like that in Brazil are just disgusting the way they treat their people. Scary. Honestly thought this was heavily emotional - the acting across the board was top notch, and helped me feel every emotion on the board. Fernanda Torres shines in her role as Eunice; an absolute powerhouse performance. Loved Mikey Maddison in Anora, but this was the performance of the year for me. No doubts there. Shame she didn’t take it. Critics’ tastes never fail to baffle me. The first half of this film is one of the most gripping of 2024. Eyes glued to the screen, incredibly tight screenplay keeping me utterly hooked and invested in the characters, and a filmmaking style to invokes a proper real-life, yet nostalgic feeling in the first 30 minutes. I thought it was so important to showcase their day to day family life in the beginning of the film - it helps make the devastation feel all that more sudden and shocking! Unfortunately after the capture situation, i feel like the film loses its way a bit, the pacing slows down quite a bit, and the interesting plot slowly fizzles out, which is a shame, because the first half of the film was incredibly written and paced. That’s the problem with real life stories - they can only be as interesting as the actual story, unless you want to manipulate events that happen, which is never a good idea. So it’s almost hard to criticise the filmmaker for this, when there’s a lack of creative freedom when adapting a true story. This was a great film though - a must watch emotional tale of grief and heartbreak. It’s not without its fun opening half hour, but don’t expect thrills and joy after that mark, it’s all depressing from there. Truly harrowing story.

Goodness gracious, I get existential about the ability to authentically portray period in films as time, technology, and civilization moves on but movies like I'm Still Here give so much reassurance and strength whilst bravely dealing with crises of their own. To process an entire generation's worth of grief under dictatorial rule is not the goal of this film, but through a somewhat high-profile example that speaks to thousands of personal histories, this film is pretty exemplary. It shows how stark and banal the backslide into this type of brutal rule can and will look like. A nation always outnumbers its government but a combination of shocking brutality, public grandstanding, collusion with corporate interests, and hoarding of resources will depress the power of any individual or small group. It's quite scary to lose the power of criticism, the gumption to inspire change in your country, or the relative simplicity of alternate viewpoints under threat of sanction, capture, and/or murder. I'm Still Here explores these consequences mostly offscreen, putting in its place the shattering of an idealized household. This property on the beach becomes a visual metaphor for Brazil in microcosm as the tumult plays out. Incredibly dark forces threaten to ruin and re-contextualize the beautiful lands you call home and yet, there's nowhere else you'd rather be, with nothing to do but try and find peace. It is noble to stand up in face of these inhumane challenges but life can be so unfair. There is no guarantee of reward or recompense. If anything, the point of a journey like this is not to be persuaded, but to be well and truly broken. Everyone possesses a personal tolerance for such things. Bravery is taking yourself over the edge without much care as to the outcome, only that there is one. Dense, deep, emotional, I'm Still Here is no easy watch per se but it is a deeply informing and affecting one, driven by Fernanda Torres's incredible performance, as well as the film's immaculate capture of Brazil's view of the coup.

Como brasileira, existe em mim um cansaço acerca dos filmes sobre a ditadura, mas porque eles geralmente fazem o caminho inverso ao que é feito por esse filme. O apelo à brutalidade fisíca geralmente reduz a mensagem dos filmes nesta temática a uma lembrança do passado violento, mas Ainda Estou Aqui esquece o excesso e explora o silêncio e vazio com sensibilidade. Além de Eunice, a protagonista da história é a violência invisível que sobrevive ao fim da ditadura. No recorte do filme, essa violência está na saudade de Rubens Paiva, mas existe em muitas outras camadas da sociedade brasileira, por isso senti um pouco a falta da escolha de abordar o trabalho social de Eunice com vítimas da ditadura de todo tipo, afinal, ela mesma sempre disse que a maior vítima era o Brasil como um todo e não uma família ou outra. Mas, de todo jeito, Ainda Estou Aqui é um filme especial por ser sobre o presente, mesmo sendo ambientando no passado que o país tenta esquecer e corre o risco de repetir.

Eyes glued to the screen, incredibly tight screenplay keeping me utterly hooked and invested in the characters, and a filmmaking style to invokes a proper real-life, yet nostalgic feeling in the first 30 minutes. I thought it was so important to showcase their day to day family life in the beginning of the film - it helps make the devastation feel all that more sudden and shocking! Unfortunately after the capture situation, i feel like the film loses its way a bit, the pacing slows down quite a bit, and the interesting plot slowly fizzles out, which is a shame, because the first half of the film was incredibly written and paced. That’s the problem with real life stories - they can only be as interesting as the actual story, unless you want to manipulate events that happen, which is never a good idea. So it’s almost hard to criticise the filmmaker for this, when there’s a lack of creative freedom when adapting a true story. This was a great film though - a must watch emotional tale of grief and heartbreak. It’s not without its fun opening half hour, but don’t expect thrills and joy after that mark, it’s all depressing from there. Truly harrowing story.

Goodness gracious, I get existential about the ability to authentically portray period in films as time, technology, and civilization moves on but movies like I'm Still Here give so much reassurance and strength whilst bravely dealing with crises of their own. To process an entire generation's worth of grief under dictatorial rule is not the goal of this film, but through a somewhat high-profile example that speaks to thousands of personal histories, this film is pretty exemplary. It shows how stark and banal the backslide into this type of brutal rule can and will look like. A nation always outnumbers its government but a combination of shocking brutality, public grandstanding, collusion with corporate interests, and hoarding of resources will depress the power of any individual or small group. It's quite scary to lose the power of criticism, the gumption to inspire change in your country, or the relative simplicity of alternate viewpoints under threat of sanction, capture, and/or murder. I'm Still Here explores these consequences mostly offscreen, putting in its place the shattering of an idealized household. This property on the beach becomes a visual metaphor for Brazil in microcosm as the tumult plays out. Incredibly dark forces threaten to ruin and re-contextualize the beautiful lands you call home and yet, there's nowhere else you'd rather be, with nothing to do but try and find peace. It is noble to stand up in face of these inhumane challenges but life can be so unfair. There is no guarantee of reward or recompense. If anything, the point of a journey like this is not to be persuaded, but to be well and truly broken. Everyone possesses a personal tolerance for such things. Bravery is taking yourself over the edge without much care as to the outcome, only that there is one. Dense, deep, emotional, I'm Still Here is no easy watch per se but it is a deeply informing and affecting one, driven by Fernanda Torres's incredible performance, as well as the film's immaculate capture of Brazil's view of the coup.

Que filme estéril. Eu realmente pensei que fosse gostar mais, até porque, como não gostei de Paprika, não ia ficar naquele nhenhenhê de “é uma cópia mal feita”. Mas é realmente uma cópia mal feita. Como alguém pega um conceito tão fértil quanto sonhos e mente e faz algo tão pouco imaginativo? Os sonhos parecem mapas de uma missão de espionagem, e não o teatro da nossa mente e dos nossos desejos mais profundos. A premissa deveria abrir espaço para o absurdo, para o subconsciente, para coisas que não obedecem à lógica, mas o filme parece ter sido feito por um executivo lendo um livro de autoajuda. É extremamente elaborado, mas quase nunca parece fértil. Estamos literalmente entrando na cabeça dos personagens, mas é difícil ter alguma simpatia por eles. Os sonhos não revelam nada profundamente particular, e todos parecem existir dentro da mesma estética fria e genérica de blockbuster. O inconsciente acaba parecendo um ambiente corporativo. E os personagens também não ajudam. Achei difícil me importar com quase qualquer um deles, e o drama do protagonista e da mulher me pareceu muito mais funcional para a trama do que realmente emocionante. A única parte que me tocou foi a do DiCaprio precisar aceitar que não pode continuar vivendo preso à imagem da mulher que perdeu, porque, de alguma maneira, isso é identificável para todo mundo. A ideia de esquecer alguém, ou, pelo menos, aceitar que a memória dessa pessoa não pode continuar controlando sua vida é genuinamente bonita. É uma pena que o filme precise de tanta maquinaria em volta para chegar a algo tão singelo. A primeira metade foi insuportável. Muito chata e sem graça, parecendo só um filme de espião com uma ideia mais interessante. A segunda metade melhora bastante, porque finalmente existe alguma tensão e a estrutura dos sonhos começa a produzir consequências de verdade, mas ainda fiquei com a sensação de estar vendo um conceito extraordinário sendo utilizado de maneira infrutífera. O final, porém, é instigante, porque finalmente existe alguma ambiguidade de verdade. Se ele está sonhando, é nota 8. Se não está, é nota 4. Como não sei, fica no meio-termo: 6/10. Porque nos sonhos, estamos juntos.

It spends a lot of time explaining the rules instead of just letting you dream. There are stretches where characters are basically explaining Inception to you. Younger you might have loved learning the rules; now you might notice how much dialogue exists purely to make the mechanics understandable 4.Hans Zimmer’s score might have aged better for me than the film itself. 5. Fischer’s storyline hit me differently this time. Arguably some of the most human material in the film belongs to the person they’re manipulating. 6. Cobb still works for me, but most of the crew feel more like pieces of the heist than actual people. 7. For something about dreams, everything feels strangely organised. 8. Que filme estéril. Eu realmente pensei que fosse gostar mais, até porque, como não gostei de Paprika, não ia ficar naquele nhenhenhê de “é uma cópia mal feita”. Mas é realmente uma cópia mal feita. Como alguém pega um conceito tão fértil quanto sonhos e mente e faz algo tão pouco imaginativo? Os sonhos parecem mapas de uma missão de espionagem, e não o teatro da nossa mente e dos nossos desejos mais profundos. A premissa deveria abrir espaço para o absurdo, para o subconsciente, para coisas que não obedecem à lógica, mas o filme parece ter sido feito por um executivo lendo um livro de autoajuda. É extremamente elaborado, mas quase nunca parece fértil. Estamos literalmente entrando na cabeça dos personagens, mas é difícil ter alguma simpatia por eles. Os sonhos não revelam nada profundamente particular, e todos parecem existir dentro da mesma estética fria e genérica de blockbuster. O inconsciente acaba parecendo um ambiente corporativo. E os personagens também não ajudam. Achei difícil me importar com quase qualquer um deles, e o drama do protagonista e da mulher me pareceu muito mais funcional para a trama do que realmente emocionante. A única parte que me tocou foi a do DiCaprio precisar aceitar que não pode continuar vivendo preso à imagem da mulher que perdeu, porque, de alguma maneira, isso é identificável para todo mundo. A ideia de esquecer alguém, ou, pelo menos, aceitar que a memória dessa pessoa não pode continuar controlando sua vida é genuinamente bonita. É uma pena que o filme precise de tanta maquinaria em volta para chegar a algo tão singelo. A primeira metade foi insuportável. Muito chata e sem graça, parecendo só um filme de espião com uma ideia mais interessante. A segunda metade melhora bastante, porque finalmente existe alguma tensão e a estrutura dos sonhos começa a produzir consequências de verdade, mas ainda fiquei com a sensação de estar vendo um conceito extraordinário sendo utilizado de maneira infrutífera. O final, porém, é instigante, porque finalmente existe alguma ambiguidade de verdade. Se ele está sonhando, é nota 8. Se não está, é nota 4. Como não sei, fica no meio-termo: 6/10. Porque nos sonhos, estamos juntos.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "negativas" (0.5–2 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews negativas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

[1] nota=0.5 estrelas:
For me, Inception is a puzzle, not cinema; a film that mistakes complexity for depth and substitutes its engineered calculations for cinematic experience. Nolan does not create dreams; he engineers them. Dream and the unconscious are reduced to a set of rules, layers, timings, instructions, and computational ticking clocks. Nolan is incapable, within the work, of allowing the real madness of dreams to take shape. Nolan does not set the unconscious and dreams free; Nolan writes a rulebook for the unconscious. The dream is not free; it has rules. The unconscious is not instinctive; it is calculable. Nolan wants to create the unconscious, but his unconscious is under control. As a result, because of Nolan’s misunderstanding of the uncontrollability of the unconscious and dreams, neither is actually created in the film. That is why the more the film talks about dreams, the less it creates dreams; the more it talks about the unconscious, the less it resembles the unconscious. As the film moves forward, more and more pieces are placed on the table: the first layer, the second layer, the third layer, time... and instead of dreaming, the viewer becomes a solver of a puzzle. As a result, watching the film is less like experiencing a world and more like solving a puzzle, and Christopher Nolan fails both at creating dreams and at creating the unconscious. Then action arrives in the film and devours everything: gunfire, chases, explosions, falling, an assault on the snowy fortress, and... as if even the unconscious in Nolan’s world cannot breathe without turning into an action sequence; a world that resembles a video game or a rule-bound action film more than a fluid and unpredictable unconscious. The visual effects are technically impressive; but being impressive, for me, is not form. The rotating hallway, the folded city, and the play with gravity, rather than becoming sensory experiences, are more like the film’s engineering calculations. It does not reach feeling and form, and does not turn into meaning. This chain does not take shape for me in Inception . Even the repeated close-ups of baby-faced DiCaprio’s face do not save anything for me. The camera repeatedly moves in close to Cobb’s face, but DiCaprio’s emotionless face remains incapable of saving the film. On the other hand, the film’s emotional center is also crushed beneath the weight of its engineered calculations. Cobb and Mal are supposed to be the heart of the film, but their grief and love often become fuel for that same mechanical narrative machine. In fact, feeling does not live within the image; rather, it has to move the puzzle forward. Feeling, instead of springing from within the image, is often a device for advancing the film’s mechanical puzzle. And this is where, for me, the film collapses. The film wants to engineer feeling. But feeling cannot be engineered. For me, cinema begins where the image can create feeling, build form, and arrive at meaning without relying on an instruction manual, but in this film, the puzzle becomes more important than the image, conceptualism moves ahead of feeling, and technique does not reach form. Ultimately, in Inception , I am faced with a work that explains dreams instead of dreaming; controls the unconscious instead of creating the unconscious; and architects the pieces of a puzzle with skill, without necessarily transforming these pieces into a living cinematic experience for the viewer. Nolan engineers the puzzle in Inception ; but in the process of engineering the puzzle, he loses cinema.

For me, Inception is a puzzle, not cinema; a film that mistakes complexity for depth and substitutes its engineered calculations for cinematic experience. Nolan does not create dreams; he engineers them. Dream and the unconscious are reduced to a set of rules, layers, timings, instructions, and computational ticking clocks. Nolan is incapable, within the work, of allowing the real madness of dreams to take shape. Nolan does not set the unconscious and dreams free; Nolan writes a rulebook for the unconscious. The dream is not free; it has rules. The unconscious is not instinctive; it is calculable. Nolan wants to create the unconscious, but his unconscious is under control. As a result, because of Nolan’s misunderstanding of the uncontrollability of the unconscious and dreams, neither is actually created in the film. That is why the more the film talks about dreams, the less it creates dreams; the more it talks about the unconscious, the less it resembles the unconscious. As the film moves forward, more and more pieces are placed on the table: the first layer, the second layer, the third layer, time... and instead of dreaming, the viewer becomes a solver of a puzzle. As a result, watching the film is less like experiencing a world and more like solving a puzzle, and Christopher Nolan fails both at creating dreams and at creating the unconscious. Then action arrives in the film and devours everything: gunfire, chases, explosions, falling, an assault on the snowy fortress, and... as if even the unconscious in Nolan’s world cannot breathe without turning into an action sequence; a world that resembles a video game or a rule-bound action film more than a fluid and unpredictable unconscious. The visual effects are technically impressive; but being impressive, for me, is not form. The rotating hallway, the folded city, and the play with gravity, rather than becoming sensory experiences, are more like the film’s engineering calculations. It does not reach feeling and form, and does not turn into meaning. This chain does not take shape for me in Inception . Even the repeated close-ups of baby-faced DiCaprio’s face do not save anything for me. The camera repeatedly moves in close to Cobb’s face, but DiCaprio’s emotionless face remains incapable of saving the film. On the other hand, the film’s emotional center is also crushed beneath the weight of its engineered calculations. Cobb and Mal are supposed to be the heart of the film, but their grief and love often become fuel for that same mechanical narrative machine. In fact, feeling does not live within the image; rather, it has to move the puzzle forward. Feeling, instead of springing from within the image, is often a device for advancing the film’s mechanical puzzle. And this is where, for me, the film collapses. The film wants to engineer feeling. But feeling cannot be engineered. For me, cinema begins where the image can create feeling, build form, and arrive at meaning without relying on an instruction manual, but in this film, the puzzle becomes more important than the image, conceptualism moves ahead of feeling, and technique does not reach form. Ultimately, in Inception , I am faced with a work that explains dreams instead of dreaming; controls the unconscious instead of creating the unconscious; and architects the pieces of a puzzle with skill, without necessarily transforming these pieces into a living cinematic experience for the viewer. Nolan engineers the puzzle in Inception ; but in the process of engineering the puzzle, he loses cinema.

Inception is a film made for the big screen. I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. I love that Christopher Nolan just decided to retro-fit this sci-fi story onto a heist narrative.  It works well! The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I get that there’s a literary reference there, but it’s a hard word for half the cast to say comfortably. But that ending is a corker! The spinning top.  The great musical swell by Hans Zimmer.

I slept on Inception, no pun intended, for quite a while before finally checking it out.  I was aware of the metaphor for filmmaking and such and some complaints that for a world set in dreams, it's rather unambitious in dealing with the unreal.  And while I'm sure more could have been done to make something more challenging and experimental, the film as is acts as a fantastic ride while being a metaphor for being Christopher Nolan, a man whose work probably keeps him from his kids. But I think part of the reason I forgive the lack of being overtly fantastical in the way that a Nightmare on Elm Street might be is that because it is about filmmaking, it is a fun heist movie exploring the idea of using the pieces and ideas a viewer already knows and how when properly utilized can be a way to bring in a new idea to the viewer.  If anything, I feel this is not what Nolan thinks he does specifically but also aspirational, in hopes of being the man who can put in a new idea.  And like a thief it needs to be done with tact so eventually the "target" and become a part of the same side, with your defenses overcome in the face of an idea baked in emotion. But if this was all "idea" it wouldn't work.  The way it works is that Nolan is a tactful and even fun filmmaker, even if the films aren't big on laughs.  It's easy to think of Nolan as a maker of blockbusters that feel more "dour" but he is actually an expert ride-crafter where the goal is to make a blockbuster that still wants to explore ideas but are also a blast to watch.

Rewatched Inception to put my thoughts in which film I thought was better- Paprika or this. Getting the record straight: Inception, despite being an exposition-heavy/slow paced film, is better overall in comparison to Paprika. My opinion why is this: First off, Inception has that sort of style in which everything is difficult, yet fairly easy to understand. It may be slow, but there are multiple visually pleasing scenes/intense action sequences that keep the audience in put, also with more actually innovative narrative that just begged to be seen. Second, paprika? One can’t deny the possible influence it had on Inception, but you also can’t deny the fact that Paprika relied more heavily on a style-over-substance approach and “dream logic” to patch up its obviously weak narrative. Many that love Paprika usually trash Inception without ever knowing that Inception at least has something to hold bound to instead of what’s basically a art-showcase. There’s too much going on to even care, especially when Paprika is already slow as hell. In a simple summary, Inception may have copied Paprika- we’ll never know, but it surely became superior to it and told a much more engrossing story than Paprika will ever be. 8/10.

Desde el principio presenta una idea muy original: entrar en los sueños de otras personas para obtener o implantar información (como es el caso en esta película). Es un concepto complejo, pero la película logra desarrollarlo de una forma que se vuelve cada vez más interesante conforme avanza la historia. Lo que más me gustó fue precisamente el concepto de los sueños, las actuaciones y los giros de trama. La forma en que Nolan construye distintos niveles de sueños y hace que todos funcionen al mismo tiempo es algo que pocas películas han intentado hacer. Leonardo DiCaprio hace una gran actuación como Cobb. Además de liderar al equipo, consigue transmitir el peso emocional que carga durante toda la historia. También me gustó mucho la dinámica que tiene con los demás miembros del grupo, ya que hace que la misión se sienta más real y que te intereses por lo que les ocurre a todos. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final. Es un momento lleno de tensión, acción y emoción donde todas las piezas de la historia comienzan a encajar. Además, la forma en que se conectan los diferentes niveles de sueños hace que la secuencia sea aún más emocionante. La música es otro de los puntos fuertes de la película. Ayuda a crear una sensación constante de misterio, urgencia y grandeza que encaja perfectamente con la historia. Algo que también me parece destacable es el uso de efectos prácticos. Nolan evitó depender completamente del CGI y utilizó escenarios reales, efectos físicos y cámaras IMAX para muchas secuencias importantes. Esto hace que escenas como los pasillos giratorios o los cambios de gravedad se sigan viendo espectaculares incluso años después de su estreno. Una película inteligente, emocionante y visualmente espectacular que demuestra por qué Christopher Nolan es uno de los directores más importantes.

Inception is a film made for the big screen. I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. I love that Christopher Nolan just decided to retro-fit this sci-fi story onto a heist narrative.  It works well! The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I get that there’s a literary reference there, but it’s a hard word for half the cast to say comfortably. But that ending is a corker! The spinning top.  The great musical swell by Hans Zimmer.

I slept on Inception, no pun intended, for quite a while before finally checking it out.  I was aware of the metaphor for filmmaking and such and some complaints that for a world set in dreams, it's rather unambitious in dealing with the unreal.  And while I'm sure more could have been done to make something more challenging and experimental, the film as is acts as a fantastic ride while being a metaphor for being Christopher Nolan, a man whose work probably keeps him from his kids. But I think part of the reason I forgive the lack of being overtly fantastical in the way that a Nightmare on Elm Street might be is that because it is about filmmaking, it is a fun heist movie exploring the idea of using the pieces and ideas a viewer already knows and how when properly utilized can be a way to bring in a new idea to the viewer.  If anything, I feel this is not what Nolan thinks he does specifically but also aspirational, in hopes of being the man who can put in a new idea.  And like a thief it needs to be done with tact so eventually the "target" and become a part of the same side, with your defenses overcome in the face of an idea baked in emotion. But if this was all "idea" it wouldn't work.  The way it works is that Nolan is a tactful and even fun filmmaker, even if the films aren't big on laughs.  It's easy to think of Nolan as a maker of blockbusters that feel more "dour" but he is actually an expert ride-crafter where the goal is to make a blockbuster that still wants to explore ideas but are also a blast to watch.
