[1] nota=2.5 estrelas:
I enjoyed the dialogue quite a bit! The story itself was good but nothing out of this world. I didn't care much for the characters. I got left wanting more.

[2] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Cut an hour off and it's an entertaining western, but as it stands, "The Hateful Eight" is boring as hell, extremely long yet underdeveloped, but at the same time funny, beautifully scored and shot, and well acted. Also, a bit sexist and a little bit indulgent with the depiction of racism. Not a fan of the pointless flashback, some of the cast, and the redundant narration that happens twice.

[3] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Man this is the third time I've tried watching this and it is just sooooo slow, I fell asleep all three times 😔. I want to like it so bad but I just can't...

[4] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Gereğinden fazla kan ve şiddet anlatının önüne geçiyor ve çoğu zaman doğrudan bir katkısı yok. Filmi sahnelere ayırmakta pek bir şey katmamış bence. Anladık yönetmen tarzı falan ama yani atmosfer ve oyunculuk dışı bir şey yok o da sadece bütçe ile alakalı zaten genel anlamda tek oda da geçti atmosferi bir zahmet yap

[5] nota=2.5 estrelas:
I think the best thing about this film is the fact that Ennio Morricone won an Oscar for the score but he used unused tracks from “the thing” which at the time received him a razzie nomination for worst score. I’ve only seen this once & that was around the time it came out, didn’t like it then & I really don’t like it now. Don’t think it’s terrible , score was a very clear standout but it’s so overlong & simply made to appease Tarantino fandom! This plays like a parody of Tarantino wether that’s the dialogue or lifted scenes from inglorious bastards, he’s tried real hard to replicate that bar scene but this films far too sloppy & self indulgent to have any balance at all really! Clearly inspired by “The thing” and I have no issue with that like do your thing but this is more riddled with convenience compared & just the one location plays like a play, wasn’t really a fan and also the politics are just lacking any substance, just adding buzz phrases throughout & trying to provoke instead of digging deep into the sociopolitical commentary of America. Think it looks absolutely amazing though & considering I think Tarantino has never really been a visual director, he’s more style & aesthetic. Think this looks great but for sure now belongs in the bottom tier of Tarantino's work!

[6] nota=2.5 estrelas:
La fotografía es increíble, el formato es alucinante, el casting es imperdible. Dura más que un documental de History Channel y es lentísima a más no poder. De no ser por el elemento fotográfico, aburre.

[7] nota=2.5 estrelas:
É lindo, mas assim que filme chato. Até o primeiro odiado (Samuel L fucking Jackson) blz, ótimo! Segundo já começou a ficar paia, depois foi péssimo acompanhar... Foi um porres os diálogos que todo mundo tanto diz, já não sabia mais quem era quem nessa história, só gostava da Mulher kkkkkkk ela era mto boa

[8] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I strongly feel like Tarantino does best in very small, focused stories like this one. You really feel the cold and the bloody clothes in this film, it’s all extremely visceral. The gore is pretty extreme, but in a story so closely linked to revenge it makes sense. There’s some fantastic acting on display here. I would say the film earns its 3 hour run time, with only some scenes in the beginning feeling too long. I give it a 3 star review because despite all my praise, I’m not really sure if it was my thing or if I’ll want to watch it again.

[9] nota=3.0 estrelas:
When a modern western set in the snow is as interesting as an ass rash that refuses to quit, yet no matter how long you scratch, it always begs for more.

[10] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I love westerns and I (unfortunately) have a soft spot for Tarantino's brand of wackiness but this is overwhelmed from beginning to end with a feeling that another director could have done more with the screenplay. After years of being recommended this by people who know my tastes, I'm happy with the parts that I really love: the Morricone score made up of scrapped concept themes for The Thing , the Dykstra visuals and Nicotero effects, the costuming and atmosphere all add up to something really fun to look at and experience. Sadly there's just a little too much of that over the top flavor that muddles the enjoyability for me, it ends up being less than the sum of its parts. It worked much better in Django Unchained where things felt a little more goofy by nature of the visual language and soundtrack, the QT-brand tone just doesn't do the final product any favors  I can't imagine the extended cut and it's extra 25 minutes would change my mind.

[11] nota=3.0 estrelas:
C’est sûrement le film de Tarantino que j’apprécie le moins de ceux que j’ai vus, malgré que j’ai beaucoup aimé le début et la tension qu’il y avait entre chaque personnage était très intéressante, mais j’ai trouvé que, dans la suite du récit, Tarantino a voulu en faire trop, encore plus que d’habitude ce qui m’a un peu sorti de l’histoire et a détruit un peu la tension qui régnait. Globalement, je suis un peu déçu de ce film, car j’ai beaucoup aimé le départ du celui-ci et ce qu’il installe, mais j’ai trouvé la suite peu intéressante avec de la violence inutile. Là où dans certains de ses films cette violence renforce le scénario et l’histoire, dans celui-là, je l’ai trouvée mal maîtrisée et poussée trop loin pour n’apporter rien aux scénario ceux qui nuit a l’histoire malheureusement.

[12] nota=3.0 estrelas:
After seeing the totality of Tarantino’s works, I think this may have been the weakest of the bunch. I am a fan of outlaw/cowboy-esque films, and similar to Django Unchained, there was the whole bounty hunting spiel. I think this was a little too similar to the plot, and it felt a little too dialogue heavy. I got bored midway through the film not in a bad way but more of a “can this hurry up and get to the meat of the story”. The ending was honestly the redeeming part, same with Samuel L. Jackson’s slomo of calling her a bitch, to which I had to laugh so hard. Good film, just not my favorite from him.

[13] nota=3.0 estrelas:
God damn it, from the moment Chris (Goggins) appeared on my screen until the very last minute, I was entertained.His acting was top notch. He was the only one that was making me laugh HAHAHAHAHAH, despite everything, he is such a kid like he just wanted to be involved and when he gets the chance he was so happy and you could literally see him wants to fly from happiness HAHAHAHAHAHA. Oh God i think he was my fav (nasty ass) character between all these (nasty ass) characters. And now with my raking for every Tarantino film I've watched so far: 1- kill bill 2- inglorious basterds 3- django unchained 4- the hatful eight 5- pulp fiction 6- once upon a time in Hollywood

[14] nota=3.0 estrelas:
there were some REALLY cool parts and some REALLY shit parts. it made sense why the n word count was so high once i realised quentin had written the movie as well as directed. a man so insufferable that fiona apple considered sobriety. the twist wasn’t as awesome as i thought it would be. i grew up on midsomer murders and law and order and found this quite underwhelming. i did enjoy the repetitive nature of the nailing of the door. the stew looked delicious, as did the coffee. there was no blizzard at my house last night but i was cold and i made soup and mulled wine. the guy who plays joe gage or the grouch was very hard to take seriously, that hair was horrendous. that’s it really.

[15] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Muy buen guion, muy bien ambientada. Para mi gusto, demasiado larga y lenta, pero buen final y dentro de todo está bueno ver películas de este estilo, que involucran al espectador y van a cierto ritmo en el cual te permite dudar de todo e incluso formar tus propias teorías, mi error fue esperar algo diferente, pero creo que la película en sí, está muy bien lograda, es la primera de Tarantino que veo. Red dead redemption is here👏🏻🤓 No la volvería a ver, pero creo que si la recomiendo.

[16] nota=3.0 estrelas:
There are a lot of really great things about this movie but also a lot of times I asked myself "what was the point?" and the answer is there is none. this is a movie that's proud of having nothing to say. it just wants to be gritty and soulless and mean. that's not worth nothing but not enough to make it great

[17] nota=3.0 estrelas:
A extended period piece version of Reservoir Dogs mixed with the bar scene in Inglorious Basterds.... I like QT but watching all his work in a row makes you realise how little he's grown he had one of the best directorial starts yet yet his writing never grew up with him

[18] nota=3.0 estrelas:
cool cast, great acting, and beautiful cinematography, but lowkey boring and way too many men. nothing much to say. oh, actually, there is. fuck you, tarantino.

[19] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Devo ammettere che per me Tarantino non è mai stato un grande regista, certo ho apprezzato molto tutti i suoi film ma semplicemente non trovo tutta la sua grandezza. Detto questo, The hateful eight è un perfetto quadri dell'America di ieri e di oggi, piena di contraddizioni e rancore. Bei colpi di scena, bei dialoghi, bellissima ambientazione ma manca qualcosa di importante. Manca quella scintilla che gli fa superare il 7/8, quella sensazione che stai guardando un'opera completa. Non lo so, Tarantino poteva fare molto di più.

[20] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I might not get the context about many things in the film but loved Quentin's style of conversations. Last 40 mins was too good. Man... Is this the only Quentin's film that doesn't have shot of women's feet..?

[21] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Incredible cinematography with beautiful snowy landscape shots. Historical significance with the civil war as well as the confederacy. Quite a slow burn. Betrayal and realities of such crime groups is the Tarantino specialty and this film does not disappoint especially with the star cast. A battle sharing racism seeded in historical war truths and general weirdness. An impostor tale similar to Reservoir Dogs and various murder mystery films. This is a mix of western and mafia, two of my personal least favourites. Typical Tarantino level of icky gore and violence but I do appreciate the nonlinear narrative structure. The ending twists are alright but the slow-motion speech seems out of place. The ending’s okay, nothing too wayward.

[22] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Watched with my 17 year old son (approaching Tarantino completism, for him), and I stand by everything in this review, following my first (and only prior) viewing: letterboxd.com/davidgermer/film/the-hateful-eight/ Ironically, his follow-up - Once Upon a Time - I instantly loved so much more, and it's since vaulted in my top 2 of all his movies (alongside Pulp Fiction, just ahead of Jackie Brown and Kill Bill). Like my recent rewatch of Django, what I hated about this the first time bothered me less the second time around... but I still didn't love how this ultimately ended. He is such a master at scene staging, character building, setting up (and releasing) tension, and of course, dialogue.  Too often, I just don't think he has anything worth saying, and the crux of too many of his stories are an excuse to see people do awful things to each other.

[23] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Historia y guion muy de Tarantino, con sus giros, con sus contextos, sus explicaciones… papelón de Samuel L Jackson , espectacular. Pero por lo demás, pelicula un poco difícil para mantenerte atento si eres un espectador casual, e historia un tanto larga. Aprobada aunque no descarto volver a verla

[24] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Heureusement qu'il y a le chapitre 4, sinon je pense que j'aurais abandonné. On reconnaît bien le style de Tarantino mais je ne pense pas complètement l'apprécier dans ce film.

[25] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Compelling, highly claustrophobic betrayal-revenge flick. Bit too long on the runtime but engaging and well written characters make up for it as usual in a Tarantino film. Good camera positions/blocking too but ultimately I fail to enjoy the film as much as I did with other Tarantino films.

[26] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Klappt im Rewatch nicht ehrlich. Ist wirklich einer von Tarantinos schlechteren Filmen. Zu lang. Zu behäbig. Zu cartoonig. Ein Twist, der beim 2. Mal nicht mehr gut ist. Einzig Morricones Musik und Leighs Schauspiel sind grandios.

[27] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I found myself to be interested at times, but toward the end it was great, and I like the last 40 minutes a lot. Just a messy movie with enjoyable moments.

[28] nota=3.0 estrelas:
QT’s There Will Be Blood, a violent, sadistic Western that amounts to something like an origin myth. It is easily his most alienating, least likable movie, and it competes with Django Unchained as his worst. It is baggy, self-indulgent, undisciplined filmmaking. You can sense the willful perversity behind it: It’s almost like a self-imposed challenge — how to make a 2-hour, 45-minute epic in the confines of a single location. (He fails his own challenge.) But despite my reservations, the go-for-broke, don’t-give-a-shit folly of it all earns respect, if not admiration. He knows exactly what he’s doing. I think he knows that there is not a single likable person here (see the title), that the violence is as over-the-top as it’s been in any of his movies, and that he’s pushing the limits of audience patience. He thinks his voice, his talent, his virtuosity, the power of his message, and his audience’s loyalty will carry him through. They don’t, not all the way at least.

[29] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Definitely not Tarantino’s best work but it was still a good watch. Going for a similar approach to reservoir dogs was very bold and in honesty did not work out great. He tries to reach the heights of Sergio Leone in his westerns but inevitably never will, even used Ennio in this film. The acting performances are great and so are piecing together of events but Tarantino always seems to write his stories with same or similar endings in mind. I cannot deny I enjoyed this film but it is just  very poor.

[30] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I think 8 in the title means, 80% Dialogues 10% Tension 10% Plot This could have been way crisp if it was under 2hrs, still the plot is very thin & the dialogues didn't have that much of a soul until shooting part kicks in 😮‍💨🔥.

[31] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Another action packed Tarantino flick with so much swearing and blood, but this time with a special guest.. cabin fever. Or poison, if you may. Definitely a good movie, if not outrageous. But outrageous is what Tarantindo does best, right?

[32] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Ett mordmysterium som tar slut omedelbart efter att det kommer igång och sen spårar ut i en ointressant blodig röra. Mycket att tycka om här annars, men det känns som att återigen saboteras något potentiellt väldigt bra av Tarantinos besatthet av våld och vulgaritet. Inga fötter här dock.

[33] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Beautiful looking, directing is on and off with some great compositions but an altogether waste of a frame by setting it in one place. Cha um Tatum is wasted but no other actor is. The script is one of Tarontino’s weakest but the actors find a way to draw the best out of it. Beautiful sight and sound whilst all costumes and production design make one room give it the decades of life it has.

[34] nota=3.0 estrelas:
كنت مستمتع بالجو و البناء البطيء كان عاجبني مع ان الاغلب بيشوفه ممل بس عجبني النهاية حلوه و كم حدث صادم و مع جو خارق شخصيات اقذر من بعض و عنصريين على اشكال وصخه بس مستحيل انصح ذا الفلم لاي شخص لان وربي الكعبة في مشهد في النص وربي اقرفني قرف لدرجة كنت ب استفرغ الي شاف الفلم ممكني يفهمني يا مخرج يا مازوخي يا تارنتينو تفوو عليك على المشهد الزبال كان يمديك تجيبه كسالفة بدل القرف الي شفته عشان كذا باقيمه تقييم زبال لانه قهرني كنت مستمتع سد نفسي الله يلعنه و طلعت من الجو مع ان صار الفلم امتع و افضل والله تقززت شيء قرف عشان كذا لا تتابعه او احقاقا للحق ممتع بس ذيك اللقطه قرف قرف المشكلة بس هي المقرفه

[35] nota=3.0 estrelas:
extremely well shot, paced, and edited with dialogue and direction that makes the characters all feel real. unfortunately the actual *plot* of the movie, while a good overall idea, does not progress in a believable or especially interesting way. the first hour and half or so is amazing, with a lot of heavy tension that had me tethered to the screen unable to blink, however once action begins happening, cards are revealed, and the tension is broken, the movie becomes incredibly boring. i also absolutely loathe the direction of having a confederate fighter who idolizes the confederacy and continues hunting and murdering emancipated slaves after the civil war ended team up with the freedman protagonist and becoming a good guy dueteragonist. the ending as well was very obviously intended to be a great act of catharsis, and drawn out as such, however instilled no such feeling in me.

[36] nota=3.0 estrelas:
saw about 20 min of this when it was on at a friend’s apartment one time and thought wow that’s really violent and vulgar. my opinion really hasn’t changed after seeing the entire thing, epitome of boy movie.

[37] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Le risque de développer un style de mise en scène est à la longue de s'enfermer dedans et d'en être prisonnier. Peut être que certains esprits plus fermés et ayant une très grande confiance en eux sont moins propices à la remise en question et aux changements propres à la curiosité, ce qui en découle une certaine stagnation quel que soit ce que l'on fait. Ça fait 30 ans que Tarantino répète les mêmes schémas qu'ils narratifs ou dans sa mise en scène. Déjà très marqués dès Pulp fiction, j'ai l'impression que l'on atteint le plus haut dans Kill Bill. Depuis j'ai cette sensation de plus en plus présente dès Inglorious Bastard de revoir les mêmes mécaniques avec seul un décors en toile de fond qui changeait. Si dans ce dernier, cela passait encore, cette impression dérangeante s'est accentuée dans Jango. Ici avec Hateful Eight, cela en est presque une caricature de son propre style, tout devient trop un Déjà Vu et même les dialogues, souvent riches chez Tarantino sont un peu en deçà. Le film demeure agréable et sympathique mais je certaine lassitude l'emporte. Il a néanmoins rompu avec ce style avec Once upon a Time in Hollywood, ce que j'avais apprécié, même si il s'est rappelé à lui même dans les 15 dernieres minutes.

[38] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Lo mismo que reserveir dogs, pero ahora en el antiguo america. tarda mucho en arrancar pero al menos cuando le disparan en los testículo a samuel l jackson vale la pena verla

[39] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Está muy bien Samuel Jackson pero la película muy meh. La estética y ambientación me gustó, como se usa el idioma de la época también pero me quedo con poco más. Tiene un buen sentido del humor y que esté dividida por capítulos al principio es medio raro pero después está bueno.

[40] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Better on second rewatch this year and third or fourth overall due to plot and some of the acting but still a bit too gory and disgusting with the one confederate's son scene. I'd rather this currently still at the very bottom of Tarantino's filmography (but haven't yet seen Kill Bill (or haven't in awhile) or Jackie Brown). Like how the movie ends though.

Don’t think it’s terrible , score was a very clear standout but it’s so overlong & simply made to appease Tarantino fandom! This plays like a parody of Tarantino wether that’s the dialogue or lifted scenes from inglorious bastards, he’s tried real hard to replicate that bar scene but this films far too sloppy & self indulgent to have any balance at all really! Clearly inspired by “The thing” and I have no issue with that like do your thing but this is more riddled with convenience compared & just the one location plays like a play, wasn’t really a fan and also the politics are just lacking any substance, just adding buzz phrases throughout & trying to provoke instead of digging deep into the sociopolitical commentary of America. Think it looks absolutely amazing though & considering I think Tarantino has never really been a visual director, he’s more style & aesthetic. Think this looks great but for sure now belongs in the bottom tier of Tarantino's work!

[10] nota=3.0 estrelas:
I love westerns and I (unfortunately) have a soft spot for Tarantino's brand of wackiness but this is overwhelmed from beginning to end with a feeling that another director could have done more with the screenplay. After years of being recommended this by people who know my tastes, I'm happy with the parts that I really love: the Morricone score made up of scrapped concept themes for The Thing , the Dykstra visuals and Nicotero effects, the costuming and atmosphere all add up to something really fun to look at and experience. Sadly there's just a little too much of that over the top flavor that muddles the enjoyability for me, it ends up being less than the sum of its parts. It worked much better in Django Unchained where things felt a little more goofy by nature of the visual language and soundtrack, the QT-brand tone just doesn't do the final product any favors  I can't imagine the extended cut and it's extra 25 minutes would change my mind.

[28] nota=3.0 estrelas:
QT’s There Will Be Blood, a violent, sadistic Western that amounts to something like an origin myth. It is easily his most alienating, least likable movie, and it competes with Django Unchained as his worst. It is baggy, self-indulgent, undisciplined filmmaking. You can sense the willful perversity behind it: It’s almost like a self-imposed challenge — how to make a 2-hour, 45-minute epic in the confines of a single location. (He fails his own challenge.) But despite my reservations, the go-for-broke, don’t-give-a-shit folly of it all earns respect, if not admiration. He knows exactly what he’s doing. I think he knows that there is not a single likable person here (see the title), that the violence is as over-the-top as it’s been in any of his movies, and that he’s pushing the limits of audience patience. He thinks his voice, his talent, his virtuosity, the power of his message, and his audience’s loyalty will carry him through. They don’t, not all the way at least.

[37] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Le risque de développer un style de mise en scène est à la longue de s'enfermer dedans et d'en être prisonnier. Peut être que certains esprits plus fermés et ayant une très grande confiance en eux sont moins propices à la remise en question et aux changements propres à la curiosité, ce qui en découle une certaine stagnation quel que soit ce que l'on fait. Ça fait 30 ans que Tarantino répète les mêmes schémas qu'ils narratifs ou dans sa mise en scène. Déjà très marqués dès Pulp fiction, j'ai l'impression que l'on atteint le plus haut dans Kill Bill. Depuis j'ai cette sensation de plus en plus présente dès Inglorious Bastard de revoir les mêmes mécaniques avec seul un décors en toile de fond qui changeait. Si dans ce dernier, cela passait encore, cette impression dérangeante s'est accentuée dans Jango. Ici avec Hateful Eight, cela en est presque une caricature de son propre style, tout devient trop un Déjà Vu et même les dialogues, souvent riches chez Tarantino sont un peu en deçà. Le film demeure agréable et sympathique mais je certaine lassitude l'emporte. Il a néanmoins rompu avec ce style avec Once upon a Time in Hollywood, ce que j'avais apprécié, même si il s'est rappelé à lui même dans les 15 dernieres minutes.

There is a total lack of correlation and wisdom in the use of the genre. The original Spaghetti Western, the one by Sergio Leone, Sergio Corbucci, or Giulio Questi, was never just about style or "nice guys shooting." It was a cinema of urgency, dry, operatic, born from a profound disillusionment with postwar Europe, where violence reflected a world devoid of God, laws, and homeland, where silence and the desert spoke louder than dialogue. Tarantino does the exact opposite: he suffocates the Western with his own filming style, transforming what should be a visceral genre into an exercise in verbal self-indulgence. The Hateful Eight fails at its core because it rejects the space of the Western to enclose itself in a filmed, claustrophobic, and chatty play, where the "who's who" dynamic inside a snow cabin resembles more an Agatha Christie mystery rewritten with profanity than the mythical rawness of a frontier classic. The characters are not ambiguous and fascinating anti-heroes in the vein of the classics; they are merely corrugated cardboard puppets, hateful and cynical by decree, created to deliver endless monologues that attempt to sound profound but only reveal a director held hostage by his own mannerisms. There is no moral sense in Tarantino's violence here. While in the Spaghetti Western the brutality was tragic, dirty, and heavy, in The Hateful Eight it becomes merely recreational, a gratuitous and nihilistic gore spectacle that loses all cathartic force. In trying to merge the political legacy of the American Civil War with the cynicism of the European Western, Tarantino ends up getting nowhere. The film drags on at an indulgent three-hour pace, where the tension never translates into real dramatic weight, just a predictable body count. It is cinema transformed into a theme park for the director himself, proving that, to make a good Western, it is not enough to have a gigantic collection of references in the archives; It's necessary to understand the mechanics of silence, the solitude of the horizon, and the gravity of a body falling to the ground. Portuguese & English review Portuguese- Tarantino nunca conseguiu chegar a fazer um bom western nas suas tentativas, acaba por não haver uma compreensão de que o seu género de filmar quer realmente chegar ao com Django Unchained e The Hateful Eight, não há realmente uma correlação ou sensatez na utilização do Spaghetti Western. ​O grande problema destas tentativas de Tarantino, tanto em Django Unchained (2012) de forma mais gritante, como em The Hateful Eight, é que o realizador parece acreditar que fazer um Spaghetti Western se resume a decalcar a banda sonora de Ennio Morricone, usar lentes anamórficas de 70mm, filmar planos de pormenor de armas a saírem do coldre e carregar na violência hiperbolizada. Há uma total ausência de correlação e sensatez na utilização do género. O Spaghetti Western original aquele de Sergio Leone, Sergio Corbucci ou Giulio Questi nunca foi apenas sobre o estilo ou sobre "gajos fixes a disparar" era um cinema de urgência, seco, operático, que nascia de uma profunda desilusão do pós-guerra europeu, onde a violência era o reflexo de um mundo desprovido de Deus, de leis e de pátria, onde o silêncio e o deserto falavam mais do que os diálogos. ​Tarantino faz exatamente o oposto: ele sufoca o Western com o seu próprio estilo de filmar, transformando o que deveria ser um género visceral num exercício de autocomplacência verbal. The Hateful Eight falha na raiz porque renega o espaço do Western para se fechar numa peça de teatro filmada, claustrofóbica e tagarela, onde a dinâmica de "quem é quem" dentro duma cabana de neve se assemelha mais a um mistério de Agatha Christie reescrito com palavrões do que à crueza mítica de um clássico da fronteira. As personagens não são anti-heróis ambíguos e fascinantes na linha dos clássicos são apenas bonecos de cartão-canelado, odiosos e cínicos por decreto, criados para debitar monólogos intermináveis que tentam soar profundos mas que apenas revelam um realizador refém do seu próprio maneirismo. ​Não há sensatez moral na violência de Tarantino aqui. Enquanto no Spaghetti Western a brutalidade era trágica, suja e pesada, em The Hateful Eight ela torna-se meramente recreativa, um espetáculo gore gratuito e niilista que perde toda a força catártica. Ao tentar fundir a herança política da Guerra Civil Americana com o cinismo do Western europeu, Tarantino acaba por não chegar a lado nenhum. O filme arrasta-se num ritmo indulgente de três horas, onde a tensão nunca se traduz em peso dramático real, apenas numa contagem de corpos previsível. É o cinema transformado num parque de diversões temático para o próprio realizador, provando que, para se fazer um bom Western, não basta ter em arquivo uma gigantesca coleção de referências; é preciso compreender a mecânica do silêncio, a solidão do horizonte e a gravidade de um corpo que tomba no chão. English- Tarantino never managed to make a good Western in his attempts, ultimately failing to understand what his genre of filmmaking really wants to achieve with Django Unchained and The Hateful Eight; there's really no correlation or common sense in the use of the Spaghetti Western. The big problem with Tarantino's attempts, both in Django Unchained (2012), most glaringly, and in The Hateful Eight, is that the director seems to believe that making a Spaghetti Western boils down to using Ennio Morricone's soundtrack, employing 70mm anamorphic lenses, filming close-ups of guns being drawn from holsters, and relying heavily on hyperbolized violence. There is a total lack of correlation and wisdom in the use of the genre. The original Spaghetti Western, the one by Sergio Leone, Sergio Corbucci, or Giulio Questi, was never just about style or "nice guys shooting." It was a cinema of urgency, dry, operatic, born from a profound disillusionment with postwar Europe, where violence reflected a world devoid of God, laws, and homeland, where silence and the desert spoke louder than dialogue. Tarantino does the exact opposite: he suffocates the Western with his own filming style, transforming what should be a visceral genre into an exercise in verbal self-indulgence. The Hateful Eight fails at its core because it rejects the space of the Western to enclose itself in a filmed, claustrophobic, and chatty play, where the "who's who" dynamic inside a snow cabin resembles more an Agatha Christie mystery rewritten with profanity than the mythical rawness of a frontier classic. The characters are not ambiguous and fascinating anti-heroes in the vein of the classics; they are merely corrugated cardboard puppets, hateful and cynical by decree, created to deliver endless monologues that attempt to sound profound but only reveal a director held hostage by his own mannerisms. There is no moral sense in Tarantino's violence here. While in the Spaghetti Western the brutality was tragic, dirty, and heavy, in The Hateful Eight it becomes merely recreational, a gratuitous and nihilistic gore spectacle that loses all cathartic force. In trying to merge the political legacy of the American Civil War with the cynicism of the European Western, Tarantino ends up getting nowhere. The film drags on at an indulgent three-hour pace, where the tension never translates into real dramatic weight, just a predictable body count. It is cinema transformed into a theme park for the director himself, proving that, to make a good Western, it is not enough to have a gigantic collection of references in the archives; It's necessary to understand the mechanics of silence, the solitude of the horizon, and the gravity of a body falling to the ground. Still a little better than Django Unchained.

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):
{

Wow, this movie is something else. I honestly didn't know what to expect going into The Hateful Eight, but I ended up really enjoying it. The movie is pretty slow at first, but I think that's what makes it work. Most of it takes place inside one cabin, with a bunch of strangers who don't trust each other. As the movie goes on, you start questioning everyone and wondering who's actually telling the truth. The line “I’m gonna get you” really fits the feeling of the movie because you constantly feel like someone is about to turn on someone else. The dialogue is probably my favorite part. There isn't always a lot happening, but the conversations are so interesting that I didn't really mind. Tarantino can make people sitting around a table talking feel more intense than an action scene. The characters are constantly trying to figure each other out, and that paranoia keeps building. I also really liked the setting. The snow and the huge amount of isolation make the whole movie feel trapped. They're stuck together with nowhere to go, which makes the tension even better. The cabin almost feels like its own character. The characters are also just crazy 😭. Pretty much everyone is a terrible person in some way, so you don't really know who to root for. Like the movie says, “No one’s gonna be leaving this place alive.” At that point, you already know things are about to go completely off the rails. Overall, The Hateful Eight is definitely a slow burn, but once it gets going, it's really entertaining. The dialogue, characters, setting, and mystery all work together really well. It's definitely worth watching if you're into Tarantino movies.

I do rather like The Hateful Eight, but it is my least favorite Tarantino film. While it is very violent, it almost feels goofy compared to some of his other movies (especially his earlier movies which often have real darkness and depth to them), and really leans into his more playful side, with comically over the top dialogue and blood, silly voiceovers and slow-motion effects, and a more laid-back vibe than his usual movies that feel like they have a lot more gravitas. This is my first time watching it, but I do feel like I will find this to be QT's least rewatchable film. I love how you can run his movies back and enjoy them just as much, if not more, the second time, but with this one I don't think I'll be compelled to return to it as much, largely because it's just a weaker, far more self-indulgent and dialogue-heavy movie than most of his other films, but all the characters are pretty much awful people (except Zoe Bell's minor character, love her), so there's not really anyone to root for in the movie. I don't know, I did really enjoy The Hateful 8 but it's definitely his least compelling film. I loved the wintry cinematography and remote cabin setting, and the variation of characters and performances, especially Walton Goggins and Jennifer Jason Leigh, but while it is quite enjoyable and a perfectly good western, it's Tarantino's least serious and worst movie.

This was my third to last Tarantino movie, and I was honestly surprised to still see him pulling out new tricks. It felt like Reservoir Dogs if I had dosed peyote before watching. The Hateful Eight was the complete opposite from the movie I was expecting, being the most cynical spaghetti western which revels in its simplicity and is a character piece through and through. I was pleased to find that, despite the runtime and despite the minimalistic approach, I was never bored. This is one of, if not Tarantino’s funniest movie, with some of his best dialogue. It has a really strong cast in general, but the three that shone the most for me was the master manipulator Major Warren, the oblivious Sheriff Mannix, and the feral opportunist Daisy Domergue. The catalyst of the conflict being a pot of coffee that sends a chain reaction of madness and killing is true Tarantino fashion. If I had to pull away one complaint, it would be that it’s a little too straightforward for its own good. While Reservoir Dogs actively had me pulling my hair out trying to connect the dots, here there was a mix of scenes I found predictable, and scenes that threw me for a loop. But then again, maybe that’s the point. Either way I found more enjoyment in the whacky characters and slapstick brutality than the whodunnit aspect.

Tension boils in the shelter of a blizzard, a gaggle of mysterious western icons, two bounty hunters with contrasting ethics, many racists on varying degrees of the hatred spectrum, a suave British hangman with an iron grip on justice, all packed into one perfect thriller. As obtuse and aggressive as Tarantino can be, in spite of his repugnant attitude, he compensates his behaviour with the sublimeness of his character creations. The Hateful Eight is a later instalment of Quentin’s, and it shows with the challenging dynamic of this whodunnit style thriller. The Hateful Eight is like a heartfelt serenade of the entire western genre, every moment is smothered in history and every actor wears their character in the snug confines of this time period. The ensemble are the familiar faces of Tarantino’s career, with Jennifer Jason Leigh joining the ride in her fantastically devilish outlaw Daisy Domergue. The dialogue of this film is filled with fantastic nuances and character quirks, the film is very much a masterclass in characterisation, with every character introduction playing off unique and grandiose. For a near 3 hour film, The Hateful Eight wastes no time, plowing through the snow and the plot slowly bubbling up to a chemical explosion of Tarantino mayhem. It’s as if his films have a promise, to get as bloody as possible after a long, intense grind of cake cutting tension. This film is a flawless concept with so many intricacies to digest. Samuel L Jackson is as funny as ever, Walton Goggins even more so, Jennifer Jason Leigh displays all her talents, and Kurt Russell demands your attention every second. The final chapter of this film is one of the most joyous experiences I’ve ever had in the cinema. Everyone laughed and cringed at all the right moments. The final chapter is truly a spectacular piece of dark comedy that signs the movie out on a bleakly humorous and then rounds everything with a truly sweet palate cleanser of an ending. This movie is absolute perfection. It’s a modern classic with all the trimmings of a pure Tarantino quest, lead down a red stained path, all the way to a trigger happy stand off.

Wow, this movie is something else. I honestly didn't know what to expect going into The Hateful Eight, but I ended up really enjoying it. The movie is pretty slow at first, but I think that's what makes it work. Most of it takes place inside one cabin, with a bunch of strangers who don't trust each other. As the movie goes on, you start questioning everyone and wondering who's actually telling the truth. The line “I’m gonna get you” really fits the feeling of the movie because you constantly feel like someone is about to turn on someone else. The dialogue is probably my favorite part. There isn't always a lot happening, but the conversations are so interesting that I didn't really mind. Tarantino can make people sitting around a table talking feel more intense than an action scene. The characters are constantly trying to figure each other out, and that paranoia keeps building. I also really liked the setting. The snow and the huge amount of isolation make the whole movie feel trapped. They're stuck together with nowhere to go, which makes the tension even better. The cabin almost feels like its own character. The characters are also just crazy 😭. Pretty much everyone is a terrible person in some way, so you don't really know who to root for. Like the movie says, “No one’s gonna be leaving this place alive.” At that point, you already know things are about to go completely off the rails. Overall, The Hateful Eight is definitely a slow burn, but once it gets going, it's really entertaining. The dialogue, characters, setting, and mystery all work together really well. It's definitely worth watching if you're into Tarantino movies.

This was my third to last Tarantino movie, and I was honestly surprised to still see him pulling out new tricks. It felt like Reservoir Dogs if I had dosed peyote before watching. The Hateful Eight was the complete opposite from the movie I was expecting, being the most cynical spaghetti western which revels in its simplicity and is a character piece through and through. I was pleased to find that, despite the runtime and despite the minimalistic approach, I was never bored. This is one of, if not Tarantino’s funniest movie, with some of his best dialogue. It has a really strong cast in general, but the three that shone the most for me was the master manipulator Major Warren, the oblivious Sheriff Mannix, and the feral opportunist Daisy Domergue. The catalyst of the conflict being a pot of coffee that sends a chain reaction of madness and killing is true Tarantino fashion. If I had to pull away one complaint, it would be that it’s a little too straightforward for its own good. While Reservoir Dogs actively had me pulling my hair out trying to connect the dots, here there was a mix of scenes I found predictable, and scenes that threw me for a loop. But then again, maybe that’s the point. Either way I found more enjoyment in the whacky characters and slapstick brutality than the whodunnit aspect.

Tension boils in the shelter of a blizzard, a gaggle of mysterious western icons, two bounty hunters with contrasting ethics, many racists on varying degrees of the hatred spectrum, a suave British hangman with an iron grip on justice, all packed into one perfect thriller. As obtuse and aggressive as Tarantino can be, in spite of his repugnant attitude, he compensates his behaviour with the sublimeness of his character creations. The Hateful Eight is a later instalment of Quentin’s, and it shows with the challenging dynamic of this whodunnit style thriller. The Hateful Eight is like a heartfelt serenade of the entire western genre, every moment is smothered in history and every actor wears their character in the snug confines of this time period. The ensemble are the familiar faces of Tarantino’s career, with Jennifer Jason Leigh joining the ride in her fantastically devilish outlaw Daisy Domergue. The dialogue of this film is filled with fantastic nuances and character quirks, the film is very much a masterclass in characterisation, with every character introduction playing off unique and grandiose. For a near 3 hour film, The Hateful Eight wastes no time, plowing through the snow and the plot slowly bubbling up to a chemical explosion of Tarantino mayhem. It’s as if his films have a promise, to get as bloody as possible after a long, intense grind of cake cutting tension. This film is a flawless concept with so many intricacies to digest. Samuel L Jackson is as funny as ever, Walton Goggins even more so, Jennifer Jason Leigh displays all her talents, and Kurt Russell demands your attention every second. The final chapter of this film is one of the most joyous experiences I’ve ever had in the cinema. Everyone laughed and cringed at all the right moments. The final chapter is truly a spectacular piece of dark comedy that signs the movie out on a bleakly humorous and then rounds everything with a truly sweet palate cleanser of an ending. This movie is absolute perfection. It’s a modern classic with all the trimmings of a pure Tarantino quest, lead down a red stained path, all the way to a trigger happy stand off.

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):
{
  "bucket": "<nome>",
  "temas": [
    {
      "tema": "<curto>",
      "mencoes_aproximadas": <int>,
      "n_reviews_analisadas": <int>,
      "exemplo_parafraseado": "<paráfrase>"
    }
  ],
  "observacao_geral": "<1-2 frases>"
}

Not once does this movie stop to ask if you are ok. It forces you to accept Norse theology (although gruesome) in order to understand the characters. Even until the final scene, the movie does not once question the beliefs of those it is betraying. This makes the film feel like it is being told to you from a storyteller in 900 AD. That being said, one of the greatest rules of storytelling is broken. Amleth has no character arc, nor does he learn any sort of lesson. He is told at the beginning of his life what his fait is, and that is exactly what ends up happening to him. This feels natural, in fact the story wouldn't make sense if it were any other way. Amleth wouldn't truly be who he is portrayed as if it weren't for his adherence to his Norse ideologies. This got me thinking on The Oddesy. This story was told very differently and Odyseus almost feels out of place in his world. These two films represent the two different ways to tell an old story. The Oddysey is a modernized version of a story that feels relatable, while The Northman is a no-apologies telling of a story that stays honest (although not fully based on a historical story). It seems unfair to compare this to a Nolan film but boy does it hold its ground well.

That being said, one of the greatest rules of storytelling is broken. Amleth has no character arc, nor does he learn any sort of lesson. He is told at the beginning of his life what his fait is, and that is exactly what ends up happening to him. This feels natural, in fact the story wouldn't make sense if it were any other way. In the grand scheme of things, its the same as the first movie (Spongebob wants to be a “man”, adventure ensues) but with a different assortment of supporting characters. As it is with most things that follows in the foot steps of a former masterpiece, it obviously is nowhere near as great in basically every single category, except for potentially its visuals which i think is a fun mix of stylized 3D, mixed media, live action and some particularly crappy, but funny green screen segments. Having said that, I hesitate to praise its visuals, as it was clear that several assets like posters, videos, paintings and other background elements were created with AI which to me betrays a much worse and concerning core of the movie. Funnily enough it showed a TMNT shortfilm (the mutant mayhem one) before the movie, in which the characters fight AI and learn to dislike it… I guess thats the world we live in. All ln all, funny, not bad, but chasing something it doesn’t surpass, on well trotten ground, and most likely rotten to the core.

[17] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Si me preguntan por uno de mis primeros recuerdos en una sala de cine, inevitablemente aparece la primera película de Bob Esponja. La recuerdo con un cariño inmenso, ligada a esos miércoles de cine con mi mamá donde intercambiábamos tapas de gaseosa para conseguir la entrada a mitad de precio. Por eso, mi conexión con esta cinta es, en su gran mayoría, pura y vibrante nostalgia. La película logra rescatar la esencia del humor absurdo de las primeras temporadas de la serie, ese estilo que realmente te atrapa. Bob sigue siendo ese personaje noble, ingenuo y un poco tonto que a menudo es manipulado por los demás, pero que nunca pierde su esencia. Además, el slapstick —el humor de golpes y situaciones físicas extremas— funciona a la perfección; admitámoslo: ver sufrir a Calamardo es algo que, por alguna razón, nunca deja de ser divertido. Es una película redonda para disfrutar en familia. Siempre me ha fascinado cómo integran a actores reales en este mundo submarino; esa estética que parece 'mal hecha' o intencionalmente cutre es, al mismo tiempo, lo que la hace visualmente icónica y brillante. Postdata: Sigo sin entender cómo perdieron la cuenta de cuántas veces mostraron el culo de Patricio en una sola película. xD

[19] nota=3.0 estrelas:
Even after giving this another watch, while I do still like it overall, I would still consider this to be my least favorite of the four main SpongeBob movies. And I say that because, as a longtime fan of SpongeBob, it is noticeable that the story does reuse some elements from the previous films (such as SpongeBob wanting to prove that he's not just a kid, which was part of the first film's story, the climax happening on the surface like in the second film, and characters going after SpongeBob to save him, like in the third film). Additionally, the story can be a little predictable at times, since we know that SpongeBob is being tricked by the Flying Dutchman before he reveals it to him. And lastly, like I said in my first first review of this film, the film also repeats the main flaw the first film has, which is sidelining some of the main characters of the show and only focusing on a small number of them. But even with those, there are still things to like about the film. The animation is great, the voice actors give great performances, the fight scenes are good, it has a good amount of funny moments, and it is in general a good movie to watch overall. So even if I'd still say that this is one of the weaker SpongeBob movies, I still like it overall and would say it's worth watching.

Por eso, mi conexión con esta cinta es, en su gran mayoría, pura y vibrante nostalgia. La película logra rescatar la esencia del humor absurdo de las primeras temporadas de la serie, ese estilo que realmente te atrapa. Bob sigue siendo ese personaje noble, ingenuo y un poco tonto que a menudo es manipulado por los demás, pero que nunca pierde su esencia. Además, el slapstick —el humor de golpes y situaciones físicas extremas— funciona a la perfección; admitámoslo: ver sufrir a Calamardo es algo que, por alguna razón, nunca deja de ser divertido. Es una película redonda para disfrutar en familia. Siempre me ha fascinado cómo integran a actores reales en este mundo submarino; esa estética que parece 'mal hecha' o intencionalmente cutre es, al mismo tiempo, lo que la hace visualmente icónica y brillante. Even after giving this another watch, while I do still like it overall, I would still consider this to be my least favorite of the four main SpongeBob movies. Additionally, the story can be a little predictable at times, since we know that SpongeBob is being tricked by the Flying Dutchman before he reveals it to him. And lastly, like I said in my first first review of this film, the film also repeats the main flaw the first film has, which is sidelining some of the main characters of the show and only focusing on a small number of them. But even with those, there are still things to like about the film. The animation is great, the voice actors give great performances, the fight scenes are good, it has a good amount of funny moments, and it is in general a good movie to watch overall. I am surprised to say I am endeared by this animation style— the movie looks quite nice and preserves the signature look of the show while nicely translating its visuals to 3D. Beyond the 2004 original I have not seen any other SpongeBob films, but I have seen that original many times, and clearly so have the filmmakers behind The Search for SquarePants . Many of the visual gags from that film are referenced, remixed, or reinterpreted for this movie, which I don’t have much innate objection to when they’ve been releasing new SpongeBob films at a clip of about one every five years— just long enough of a gap that the children that tuned in for their last effort have very likely outgrown the target demographic by the next. 3–5 years has long been treated as the standard for churn when it comes to IP designed for children, so who am I to judge if a joke that worked for me as a child is reworked for the next generation? What I struggle much more to forgive is the repetition of themes. In this film, the titular ‘Bob strives to be seen as a “big guy”, which is a transparent euphemism for maturity. This echoes the sponge of 24 years prior, who wished to be seen as a man. His journey in both films includes episodes obviously inspired by The Odyssey. He is manipulated into action by a scheming green villain. He briefly travels to the surface world to interact with real-life humans. The story of SpongeBob, forever unfinished, becomes a Sisyphean nightmare about a boy incapable of ever truly growing up— after all, what responsible adult would choose to live in a pineapple?

I am surprised to say I am endeared by this animation style— the movie looks quite nice and preserves the signature look of the show while nicely translating its visuals to 3D. Beyond the 2004 original I have not seen any other SpongeBob films, but I have seen that original many times, and clearly so have the filmmakers behind The Search for SquarePants . Many of the visual gags from that film are referenced, remixed, or reinterpreted for this movie, which I don’t have much innate objection to when they’ve been releasing new SpongeBob films at a clip of about one every five years— just long enough of a gap that the children that tuned in for their last effort have very likely outgrown the target demographic by the next. 3–5 years has long been treated as the standard for churn when it comes to IP designed for children, so who am I to judge if a joke that worked for me as a child is reworked for the next generation? What I struggle much more to forgive is the repetition of themes. In this film, the titular ‘Bob strives to be seen as a “big guy”, which is a transparent euphemism for maturity. This echoes the sponge of 24 years prior, who wished to be seen as a man. His journey in both films includes episodes obviously inspired by The Odyssey. He is manipulated into action by a scheming green villain. He briefly travels to the surface world to interact with real-life humans. The story of SpongeBob, forever unfinished, becomes a Sisyphean nightmare about a boy incapable of ever truly growing up— after all, what responsible adult would choose to live in a pineapple?

Don’t really have any problems with it, I kinda wish the animation was 2D but the CGI is still pretty good and cartoony, not really theatrical quality but there were plenty of funny faces and visual gags. [10] nota=3.5 estrelas:
If I had a nickel for every time Derek Drymon directed a fourth installment of a movie franchise known for zany and wacky shenanigans of colorful characters that had scripts that took some story elements from the first installments, I would have two nickels! Which isn't a lot, but it's weird that it happened twice, right? I, like a grand majority of people, have had this childlike, whimsical, hilarious, optimistic, loving, and hardworking sponge as a major part of my childhood and have even implemented his way of going about the world into our daily lives. I have watched from the first seasons, all the way up to season 12, and have watched all of his movies up to this point. Sponge on the Run has its genuine moments but is severely lacking in other important areas. Sponge Out of Water was a blast and a half adventure, but the first movie is genuinely one of my favorites, and I don't believe anything could top its humor, animation, story, spectacle, and characterization of these characters we have come to love. I have noticed that every movie was helmed by someone heavily involved throughout the show and its run. The legendary creator, Stephen Hillenburg, for the first movie, the showrunner for the show when Hillenburg left after the first few seasons, Paul Tibbit for SOoW, and the co-developer of the show, Tim Hill, for SOTR. Now we have come to this movie, helmed by Derek Drymon, the creative director for the show in its earlier seasons. I was cautiously optimistic, as I liked Drymon’s direction in the things I've seen, but I was wondering how exactly funny it would be, how exactly the cast would be characterized, and whether the plot could carry a whole movie. They also really wanted to emphasize how this movie would bring back vibes of the first iconic seasons. So they intentionally were trying to raise expectations. How did I like it? I honestly had a blast, just as much as I had with Sponge Out of Water, if I am being totally honest. If I wasn’t laughing at how surprisingly funny and zany it could get with well-timed jokes and slapstick, I was always smiling from ear to ear. I even enjoyed the plot and the story, where the BOB wants to be seen as a BIG GUY and be respected as such by being brave, especially by Mr. Krabs, one of the biggest guys he knows, so he goes along with Patrick to help the Flying Dutchman to the Underworld to prove he is indeed a BIG GUY, who was surprisingly well-acted by Mark Hamill. Not only was the comedy on point for me, but also, I really enjoyed the relationships displayed in this movie, especially the father-son dynamic with Krabs and SpongeBob. Even has a nice enough message, though I do admit it is taking a lot from the first movie and is not as well executed as it was then. The animation, while not as detailed as SOTR, is stylised in a way where it is essentially how the show looks in 3D. While this is not a perfect movie, let alone a perfect SpongeBob movie, I still had a lot of fun and even felt as happy to see SpongeBob on the big screen through this movie as I was when I was a kid rewatching the first filam an the constant reruns of episodes. So in a sense, I do feel it somewhat captured the vibes of the early seasons, just a bit. Well done, Drymon!

[10] nota=3.5 estrelas:
If I had a nickel for every time Derek Drymon directed a fourth installment of a movie franchise known for zany and wacky shenanigans of colorful characters that had scripts that took some story elements from the first installments, I would have two nickels! Which isn't a lot, but it's weird that it happened twice, right? I, like a grand majority of people, have had this childlike, whimsical, hilarious, optimistic, loving, and hardworking sponge as a major part of my childhood and have even implemented his way of going about the world into our daily lives. I have watched from the first seasons, all the way up to season 12, and have watched all of his movies up to this point. Sponge on the Run has its genuine moments but is severely lacking in other important areas. Sponge Out of Water was a blast and a half adventure, but the first movie is genuinely one of my favorites, and I don't believe anything could top its humor, animation, story, spectacle, and characterization of these characters we have come to love. I have noticed that every movie was helmed by someone heavily involved throughout the show and its run. The legendary creator, Stephen Hillenburg, for the first movie, the showrunner for the show when Hillenburg left after the first few seasons, Paul Tibbit for SOoW, and the co-developer of the show, Tim Hill, for SOTR. Now we have come to this movie, helmed by Derek Drymon, the creative director for the show in its earlier seasons. I was cautiously optimistic, as I liked Drymon’s direction in the things I've seen, but I was wondering how exactly funny it would be, how exactly the cast would be characterized, and whether the plot could carry a whole movie. They also really wanted to emphasize how this movie would bring back vibes of the first iconic seasons. So they intentionally were trying to raise expectations. How did I like it? I honestly had a blast, just as much as I had with Sponge Out of Water, if I am being totally honest. If I wasn’t laughing at how surprisingly funny and zany it could get with well-timed jokes and slapstick, I was always smiling from ear to ear. I even enjoyed the plot and the story, where the BOB wants to be seen as a BIG GUY and be respected as such by being brave, especially by Mr. Krabs, one of the biggest guys he knows, so he goes along with Patrick to help the Flying Dutchman to the Underworld to prove he is indeed a BIG GUY, who was surprisingly well-acted by Mark Hamill. Not only was the comedy on point for me, but also, I really enjoyed the relationships displayed in this movie, especially the father-son dynamic with Krabs and SpongeBob. Even has a nice enough message, though I do admit it is taking a lot from the first movie and is not as well executed as it was then. The animation, while not as detailed as SOTR, is stylised in a way where it is essentially how the show looks in 3D. While this is not a perfect movie, let alone a perfect SpongeBob movie, I still had a lot of fun and even felt as happy to see SpongeBob on the big screen through this movie as I was when I was a kid rewatching the first filam an the constant reruns of episodes. So in a sense, I do feel it somewhat captured the vibes of the early seasons, just a bit. Well done, Drymon!

[1] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Some brilliantly subtle acting here in the close ups.  The unspoken word readable in an actors facial expression is sublime. Overall I enjoyed it for a French film of its time.  It does have artistic elements, and an introspective plot.  It’s well shot and has a couple of scenes that really are great in terms of character growth. Still feels very current so has stood the test of time well.  Good stuff.

[2] nota=2.5 estrelas:
To be fair to this film, it fought a bit of an uphill battle since I just watched Fritz Lang's brilliant Destiny right before this, but I just gotta say I did not enjoy this at all. Maybe I actually just chose the wrong day to watch this because on the surface there's a lot about this film that I should love. The direction is pretty dynamic, camera movements are thoroughly planned out with some really impressive long takes, the performances are all good and the film is a classic European art house character drama. However, none of it really worked for me. The direction felt more showy than intentional most of the time. The performances were strong but I could barely tell the two male characters apart if I'm being honest. But this probably has more to do with the film's biggest weakness, which is of course its script. My god is it a drag to sit through endless scenes of these 4 boring-ass people doing mundane stuff for two hours. It all feels so inconsequential and weightless. Then there is of course the climactic moment at the titular swimming pool, which was the only genuinely pretty cool scene in the entire film, but I thought that meant the film would finally start to warp up but nope. We get to watch more paint dry for the rest of the runtime. I don't know what people see in this film. All I see in it is a failed attempt at creating one of these art house classics that were being made by the dozens at this time but this just felt fraudulent. Maybe I'll give it another shot at some point but I was really struggling to get through this.

A phone call interrupts a poolside make-out session. A thirtysomething couple, Jean-Paul (Alain Delon) and Marianne (Romy Schneider), are vacationing at a lavish Saint-Tropez villa owned by absent friends. The phone call brings to the villa two visitors. One is an old friend of theirs and an ex-lover of Marianne's, Harry (Maurice Ronet), a pop music producer. The second visitor is his eighteen-year-old daughter, Penelope, played by Jane Birken. Birken is too physically mature to pass as a teenager, but she captures some of that age's awkwardness, its sullen remoteness. Jean-Paul has questions about the romance Marianne had with Harry, long-standing questions the visit rekindles as it also conjures versions of the selves these old friends were and futures they lost. Rivalries grow. The camera lingers over tan, fit bodies, both male and female, and eyes scoping other bodies. Legs abound, Marianne and Penelope's especially, in the first hour. The music quiets down in the second hour too. That helps. The look and looking are of its era. As is the acting. The disappointments and  transgressions are transhistorical. And pools . . . "Some nights anything goes," Jean-Paul tells Penelope. "Or almost anything." Emotional engagement slips gradually away so that the final embrace contrasts brutally with the sun-drenched eroticism of the opening scene.

There is a tension in their relationship which excites Marianne: the film begins with a scene in which they are together beside the villa's swimming pool and she urges him to scratch her back. He does as she asks, but then throws her into the pool and jumps in after her. In a later scene he takes a branch and uses it to lash her bare buttocks, playfully but with a force that increases as the scene cuts away. Harry (Ronet), an old friend and record producer who was Marianne's lover before Jean-Paul, arrives for a visit, surprising the couple by bringing along his 18-year-old daughter Penelope (Birkin), whose existence they had not previously known about. Marianne, without asking Jean-Paul, invites Harry and Penelope to stay. The four stay together and Harry draws Marianne back towards him as the days go by. Taunting Jean-Paul for having given up serious writing to work in advertising, Harry drinks a great deal and throws a surprise party while Jean-Paul, a recovering alcoholic, stays sober. Meanwhile, it becomes clear that Penelope neither likes nor respects her father, whom she has barely known while growing up. She and Jean-Paul become close and spend a day alone together by the sea. That night, while the women are asleep, Harry drunkenly confronts Jean-Paul and accuses him of seducing Penelope to revenge his own shortcomings on his more successful friend. Trying to punch Jean-Paul, Harry falls into the pool and is too drunk to swim. Jean-Paul, who has also been drinking, at first stops him from climbing out of the water, then deliberately pushes Harry under and holds him down until he drowns. He covers up the crime by stripping Harry's clothes off and placing fresh trousers and a shirt at the poolside to make it look like an accident. After the funeral, a policeman, Inspector Lévêque (Crauchet), visits the house more than once. He confides to Marianne his reasons for doubting the story of an accident, that Harry had been wearing his watch, which was expensive and not waterproof, and that there is no trace of sweat on the clothes he was supposed to have been wearing. When she tells Jean-Paul, he confesses everything to her, and she goes to see Harry's clothes, hidden in the cellar, that would have given him away. But when she does not take this evidence to the police, the inspector reluctantly suspends the inquiry. Marianne takes Penelope to the airport and sees her off as she returns to her mother. When Penelope demands the truth about her father's death, Marianne assures her it really was an accident. She and Jean-Paul are then about to leave the villa when she tells him that they will not go together. She calls for a taxi but he places his hand on the telephone, cutting off her call and silencing her. In the end, neither leaves that day, and in the film's final shot they stand side by side looking out the window at the swimming pool, and then embrace.

aka: La Piscine NS Alain Delon Romy Schneider Maurice Ronet Jane Birkin Paul Crauchet FRANCE Jean-Paul (Delon), a writer, and Marianne (Schneider), his girlfriend for just over two years, are holidaying at a friend's villa near Saint-Tropez. There is a tension in their relationship which excites Marianne: the film begins with a scene in which they are together beside the villa's swimming pool and she urges him to scratch her back. He does as she asks, but then throws her into the pool and jumps in after her. In a later scene he takes a branch and uses it to lash her bare buttocks, playfully but with a force that increases as the scene cuts away. Harry (Ronet), an old friend and record producer who was Marianne's lover before Jean-Paul, arrives for a visit, surprising the couple by bringing along his 18-year-old daughter Penelope (Birkin), whose existence they had not previously known about. Marianne, without asking Jean-Paul, invites Harry and Penelope to stay. The four stay together and Harry draws Marianne back towards him as the days go by. Taunting Jean-Paul for having given up serious writing to work in advertising, Harry drinks a great deal and throws a surprise party while Jean-Paul, a recovering alcoholic, stays sober. Meanwhile, it becomes clear that Penelope neither likes nor respects her father, whom she has barely known while growing up. She and Jean-Paul become close and spend a day alone together by the sea. That night, while the women are asleep, Harry drunkenly confronts Jean-Paul and accuses him of seducing Penelope to revenge his own shortcomings on his more successful friend. Trying to punch Jean-Paul, Harry falls into the pool and is too drunk to swim. Jean-Paul, who has also been drinking, at first stops him from climbing out of the water, then deliberately pushes Harry under and holds him down until he drowns. He covers up the crime by stripping Harry's clothes off and placing fresh trousers and a shirt at the poolside to make it look like an accident. After the funeral, a policeman, Inspector Lévêque (Crauchet), visits the house more than once. He confides to Marianne his reasons for doubting the story of an accident, that Harry had been wearing his watch, which was expensive and not waterproof, and that there is no trace of sweat on the clothes he was supposed to have been wearing. When she tells Jean-Paul, he confesses everything to her, and she goes to see Harry's clothes, hidden in the cellar, that would have given him away. But when she does not take this evidence to the police, the inspector reluctantly suspends the inquiry. Marianne takes Penelope to the airport and sees her off as she returns to her mother. When Penelope demands the truth about her father's death, Marianne assures her it really was an accident. She and Jean-Paul are then about to leave the villa when she tells him that they will not go together. She calls for a taxi but he places his hand on the telephone, cutting off her call and silencing her. In the end, neither leaves that day, and in the film's final shot they stand side by side looking out the window at the swimming pool, and then embrace.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "negativas" (0.5–2 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews negativas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

I've wasted many hours on films before, but nothing like this.  I understand the average Letterboxd user likes this film, but I don't.  I did not have a good time with this film at all.  The minute I got a half hour into it, I noticed how nothing was really happening, despite getting a labeled a psychological thriller.  Most of the movie's first half felt like a romantic drama if anything, so it looked like a drag with nothing much happening.  Come to think of it, the majority of the movie was a drag too. Shit doesn't get down until the 1 hour mark, where I started getting hopeful the movie might turn around.  The 2nd half reminded me of a Alfred Hitchcock film, which is why I felt that way.  But just when I was getting into it, the hope faded away by the end and I got slapped in the face as a result.  It might me the biggest letdown I've ever seen in a thriller/crime movie.  Even Emilia Perez had some value, and that's saying a lot. I was thinking while writing this review how prior to this, I had the idea of watching an old MGM movie on Blu-ray, but the other side of my brain said to find a movie from HBO Max instead because they usually have a vast library of films.  Man, I should've just went for the MGM movie. The Swimming Pool may be good like some people here said.  Maybe I just didn't see it right according to them, but I feel like I saw enough to be absolutely baffled.  I don't care if anyone hates me for this opinion, because I'm already too stunned to fight back.

Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Um filme que captura bem a estética dos anos 1960. A sungueta estampada do Alain Delon, o vestido verde de estampa psicodélica da Romy Schneider, os quinhentos enlatados no jantar de comida oriental, a festa na casa com a cômica dança de rock n roll da época (que era o auge da modernidade)... E as cenas iniciais cheias de sol e piscina que vendem muito bem o filme até hoje. As atuações são meio engessadas, todo mundo meio duro, isso me incomoda um pouco, mas fica coerente com a proposta toda de ser um ensaio de dois homens competindo psicologicamente e simbolicamente para ver quem tem o "maio pau". Quando o cara aparece com aquele Maserati Ghibli deu para ver que, além de ter sido pedido da produção para geral poder dar um rolê em coupé esportivo durante as gravações, aquele personagem também seria o antagonista mor do filme. No mais é isso, um filme sobre a eterna temática fidelidade/traição para ver num fim de semana como uma viagem ensolarada com com hospedagem no sul da França.
