[2] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Lucrecia Martel’s Zama is one of those films where I can recognize and even respect the craft behind it without necessarily understanding the acclaim surrounding it. Martel is clearly in complete control of her direction, creating a visually striking film that feels deliberately composed and full of strange, unsettling details, while the unusual use of sound adds another layer to its atmosphere. The performances are also strong, particularly Daniel Giménez Cacho in the lead, whose restrained portrayal gives Don Diego de Zama an appropriately weary and increasingly pathetic presence. There is certainly something fascinating about the way the film captures colonial stagnation, isolation, and the absurdity of a man desperately waiting for a transfer that may never come, but for me, that fascination rarely translated into an engaging viewing experience. The narrative felt extremely uneven, with long stretches where there seemed to be very little conventional plot momentum, making the film’s nearly two-hour runtime feel considerably longer than it actually is. More importantly, I found myself emotionally distant from de Zama throughout most of the film; despite what he goes through, I simply never became invested enough in his fate for the story’s increasingly surreal developments to have much impact. I can appreciate that the sluggish pacing, ambiguity, and fragmented storytelling are intentional choices, and Martel’s filmmaking is undeniably distinctive, but intention alone didn’t make the experience particularly satisfying for me. Zama is certainly an unusual and technically accomplished film, and I understand why its visual language and unconventional approach have earned it so much praise, but I ultimately found it more interesting to admire from a distance than genuinely enjoyable or compelling to watch.

let's start off with the sound, which many of our finest critics and cinephiles have lauded. the one-and-a-half minute list of production companies at the start promises craftsmanship of the highest quality. it's not good. it is ordinary at best, ordinarily immoral at worst. it seems that people simply love when things are emphasized for them: here is a surge of creativity, intended for a purpose that does not seem incongruous with the overall subject matter, and thus we are in the hands of an auteur who startles, who controls her spectators with mastery. we are no longer content to see or hear what is only humbly in front of us. like the spaniards, we are too good for humility. now, i am unsure about something, and somebody please clarify it for me, but does martel think that cutting the frame just below the hairline achieves some sort of effect, or does she just not know where to place a camera? this is very astonishing, coming from someone who, for example, allows herself to use the mbayá as a tool for her formal allegory - the settlers have wandered off into atemporality. what spatial awareness, everything is so attentively cut, the atmospheric sounds are so immersive. so painstaking is the delineation of each sequence’s margins that martel denies characters the time that their gestures and actions require. even worse - she denies animals and the others their neutrality. the only shots that escape this deriding academicism are precisely the ones that, by some miracle (aha, martel creates miracles!), have rebelled through their own strength from the misleading disorder of a film made to be seen, and presented us with a well down to a chasm where the unknown may gaze back at us.

[9] nota=2.5 estrelas:
Can't lie. I was thoroughly disappointed this isn't actually about the battle of Zama and I'd see some war elephants and some good-ass historical epic. All my hopes crushed like Titanic when it turned out the movie's only quality is being boring (not a positive quality unfortunately). And it has SpongeBob music in 3 scenes too ('The Third Man' reference). It's a real shame all those costumes, sets and the potential for a great historical epic were wasted on a weak product. It took me 1.5 hours to realise what truly is lacking and what makes the picture so monotone - the camera almost never moves. It's static for 99% of the shots. And after experiencing so many sloggish movies recently, I finally realised this is what kills me. The camera needs to move or my head hurts.

Solo en un momento me pareció que se generaba algo más potente, cuando el gobernador le dice que la segunda carta al rey se manda 1 o 2 años despues, pero en el resto nada, en especial la relación con Luciana que es lo que peor se adapta de toda la novela. No me esperaba que Zama fuera una película tan... divertida. Por supuesto que el ritmo de las imágenes de Martel no deja que esto se convierta de lleno en una comedia, pero el patetismo de su protagonista y la serie de situaciones absurdas que debe soportar guian a través del humor una película que por otro lado tiene una estructura más bien líquida y un trasfondo oscuro. No es que no se muestren también las aberraciones de los esfuerzos colonialistas, pero cada vez que el tono ligero comienza a volverse serio, casi pesadillezco, o cada vez que el personaje de Diego Zama empieza a adquirir un aire demasiado trágico, entra la música plácida y anacrónica de Los Indios Tabajaras que le devuelven a la película una resignada ligereza, como de quien acepta, agoado, un destino inevitable. Su naturaleza de western se consolida sobre todo en el último tercio con esa exploración de tierras inhóspitas casi irreales y la confrontación con los indígenas. Hay películas que convierten la espera en el centro de su historia. Zama va un paso más allá y hace que el tiempo parezca detenido y que esa sensación termine envolviendo también al espectador. Lo más interesante no es tanto el retrato del funcionario colonial como la progresiva disolución de un sujeto que vive esperando una vida que nunca llega. Zama no fracasa porque el mundo le niegue aquello que desea, sino porque ha construido su identidad alrededor de una promesa futura. Es una película sobre el autoengaño, sobre esa tendencia tan humana a aplazar indefinidamente la propia existencia mientras imaginamos que el verdadero comienzo está siempre un poco más adelante. Aun así, la propuesta me resulta más estimulante desde un punto de vista intelectual que emocional. Admiro la precisión con la que Martel construye ese universo absurdo, casi kafkiano, pero nunca terminé de conectar del todo con él. Me quedo, sobre todo, con la idea de que el tiempo no siempre destruye por lo que hace, sino por todo aquello que nos convence de seguir esperando.

I can't say it's the source material (I haven't read the book yet) and it's definitely not the actors (who turn in some stellar performances), but this lacked Martel's usual audiovisual intelligence, settling for a staged feel that did it no favours in terms of its framing and propulsion. Zama (2017) - Een verstilde afdaling in bureaucratische waanzin, even fascinerend als uitputtend. In het laat-18e-eeuwse Spaans-koloniale Paraguay wacht Don Diego de Zama, een ambtenaar van de kroon, al jaren op een overplaatsing die maar niet komt. Terwijl de tropische hitte, sociale vernederingen en absurde machtsverhoudingen zich opstapelen, raakt zijn gevoel voor identiteit en waardigheid langzaam uitgehold. Lucrecia Martels Zama is een film die zich doelbewust onttrekt aan conventionele vertelstructuren. Het verhaal kabbelt niet zozeer voort, maar blijft hangen — net als zijn protagonist — in een toestand van permanente verwachting. Martel gebruikt geluid, kadrering en ritme om Zama’s mentale ontwrichting voelbaar te maken: stemmen dringen zich op vanuit de marge, kaders snijden lichamen half af, en gebeurtenissen lijken zich te herhalen zonder echte vooruitgang. Het resultaat is een beklemmende sfeer waarin tijd zijn grip verliest. Die aanpak is tegelijk de grootste kracht én zwakte van de film. Martels scherpe blik op koloniale machtsstructuren en mannelijke gekrenktheid is onmiskenbaar, en Daniel Giménez Cacho speelt Zama met een indrukwekkende mengeling van trots, frustratie en existentiële leegte. Maar de film vraagt veel geduld. De afstandelijke stijl en het gebrek aan narratieve houvast maken Zama soms meer een intellectuele ervaring dan een emotionele, waardoor betrokkenheid kan wegglippen. In Argentinië werd de film vooral geprezen als een gedurfde, eigenzinnige bewerking van Antonio Di Benedetto’s gelijknamige roman, en gezien als een belangrijk auteurstatement binnen de nationale cinema. Die status is begrijpelijk, maar internationaal kan Zama ook voelen als een film die zijn publiek bewust op afstand houdt. Als cinematografisch experiment en thematische meditatie is Zama intrigerend en consequent, maar de traagheid en hermetische aanpak maken het geen gemakkelijke zit. Een film om te bewonderen om zijn intenties en vorm, eerder dan om erin meegezogen te worden.

A neo-western in the sense that it portrays the overall miserability of the frontier while also being a dissection of Zama - a typical hero figure - as a frustrated individual who has long lost any sense of purpose and finally starts a voyage into nowhere. - Magistrate Zama (introduced as prying on indigenous women) labors at the outskirts of empire, an outpost so far from the administration that no payment has reached them for over a year. "His loneliness is atrocious." A legend ("man without fear") stripped bare of any glory. This is reflected in the filmmaking which is unglamorous as well ("We have no occasion for elegance here"): the place looks shoddy, the rooms very simplistic, and the costumes artificial (like the ill-fitting wigs). - Daniel Giménez Cacho delivers a fine, intense performance as the colonial administrator wrapped in boredom and longing desire. His eyes mark him as burned out, exhausted by this desolate place. - There are witty ironic touches, such as the music played to the settlers coming in to complain that they have no laborers left because they massacred all of them for trying to get away (they claim an "encomienda": "40 tame indians"). - Overall, an absurdist takedown of colonial ideology and implementation by revealing it as an administrative hell for everyone. The last third not holding up as well, making its intention more difficult to grasp despite being a further descend into confusion. No glory anywhere.

Lucrecia Martel’s Zama is one of those films where I can recognize and even respect the craft behind it without necessarily understanding the acclaim surrounding it. Martel is clearly in complete control of her direction, creating a visually striking film that feels deliberately composed and full of strange, unsettling details, while the unusual use of sound adds another layer to its atmosphere. The performances are also strong, particularly Daniel Giménez Cacho in the lead, whose restrained portrayal gives Don Diego de Zama an appropriately weary and increasingly pathetic presence. There is certainly something fascinating about the way the film captures colonial stagnation, isolation, and the absurdity of a man desperately waiting for a transfer that may never come, but for me, that fascination rarely translated into an engaging viewing experience. The narrative felt extremely uneven, with long stretches where there seemed to be very little conventional plot momentum, making the film’s nearly two-hour runtime feel considerably longer than it actually is. More importantly, I found myself emotionally distant from de Zama throughout most of the film; despite what he goes through, I simply never became invested enough in his fate for the story’s increasingly surreal developments to have much impact. I can appreciate that the sluggish pacing, ambiguity, and fragmented storytelling are intentional choices, and Martel’s filmmaking is undeniably distinctive, but intention alone didn’t make the experience particularly satisfying for me. Zama is certainly an unusual and technically accomplished film, and I understand why its visual language and unconventional approach have earned it so much praise, but I ultimately found it more interesting to admire from a distance than genuinely enjoyable or compelling to watch.

Zama (2017) - Een verstilde afdaling in bureaucratische waanzin, even fascinerend als uitputtend. In het laat-18e-eeuwse Spaans-koloniale Paraguay wacht Don Diego de Zama, een ambtenaar van de kroon, al jaren op een overplaatsing die maar niet komt. Terwijl de tropische hitte, sociale vernederingen en absurde machtsverhoudingen zich opstapelen, raakt zijn gevoel voor identiteit en waardigheid langzaam uitgehold. Lucrecia Martels Zama is een film die zich doelbewust onttrekt aan conventionele vertelstructuren. Het verhaal kabbelt niet zozeer voort, maar blijft hangen — net als zijn protagonist — in een toestand van permanente verwachting. Martel gebruikt geluid, kadrering en ritme om Zama’s mentale ontwrichting voelbaar te maken: stemmen dringen zich op vanuit de marge, kaders snijden lichamen half af, en gebeurtenissen lijken zich te herhalen zonder echte vooruitgang. Het resultaat is een beklemmende sfeer waarin tijd zijn grip verliest. Die aanpak is tegelijk de grootste kracht én zwakte van de film. Martels scherpe blik op koloniale machtsstructuren en mannelijke gekrenktheid is onmiskenbaar, en Daniel Giménez Cacho speelt Zama met een indrukwekkende mengeling van trots, frustratie en existentiële leegte. Maar de film vraagt veel geduld. De afstandelijke stijl en het gebrek aan narratieve houvast maken Zama soms meer een intellectuele ervaring dan een emotionele, waardoor betrokkenheid kan wegglippen. In Argentinië werd de film vooral geprezen als een gedurfde, eigenzinnige bewerking van Antonio Di Benedetto’s gelijknamige roman, en gezien als een belangrijk auteurstatement binnen de nationale cinema. Die status is begrijpelijk, maar internationaal kan Zama ook voelen als een film die zijn publiek bewust op afstand houdt. Als cinematografisch experiment en thematische meditatie is Zama intrigerend en consequent, maar de traagheid en hermetische aanpak maken het geen gemakkelijke zit. Een film om te bewonderen om zijn intenties en vorm, eerder dan om erin meegezogen te worden.

"Estoy haciendo con ustedes lo que nadie hizo conmigo. Les digo que no tengan esperanza" Decente película, no conecté como esperaba. "Zama" es una cinta con un apartado técnico increíble y una historia que resulta interesante en un inicio pero con la que no pude conectar del todo por su ritmo tan lento, valoro algunas cosas buenas que tiene pero no se me hicieron suficientes. Sinopsis: En el siglo XVIII, un oficial español espera con ansia ser trasladado de Asunción a Buenos Aires. Obsesionado con ello, acepta cualquier misión que se le encargue, como la de atrapar a un peligroso bandido que ha huido a un territorio inexplorado. La historia es normalita, su ritmo tan lento me mató. Una de las cosas que más le destaco es lo bien que está recreada ésta época histórica, haciendo que parezca que fue grabada en ese tiempo, teniendo una ambientación sensacional que fue de las mejores cosas. Además, su desarrollo no me parece malo, tiene algunas escenas bien realizadas y tampoco resulta predecible. Sin embargo, lo lenta que se me hizo fue increíble, dura solo dos horas pero sentí que fue mucho más, igual fue tema mío porque la película está lejísimos de ser mala, pero sentí muchas escenas innecesarias que podrían haberse recortado para un mejor ritmo. Los personajes cumplieron, lo más rescatable es el protagonista. Don Diego de Zama es el mejor personaje de todos, me gustó el desarrollo que tiene a lo largo de la historia y los cambios que va sufriendo mientras trata de obtener lo que quiere. Después hay otros personajes que no están mal y encima aportan a su desarrollo, como lo son Luciana Piñares y Vicuña Porto, sobretodo éste último. En otros aspectos destaco principalmente el trabajo de Lucrecia Martel en guion y dirección, a pesar de que no haberme gustado el ritmo que le dio me parece que hace un muy sólido trabajo en éste apartado, acompañada de una espectacular fotografía, sonido, vestuario y maquillaje para hacer que todo se vea lo más realista posible. Por último, las actuaciones son buenísimas, sobretodo la de Daniel Giménez Cacho que está brillante y mejora bastante a su personaje. En conclusión, una normalita película que siento que merece un poco más de calificación que esto pero lamentablemente no terminó de gustarme del todo, igualmente no considero que sea para todo el mundo, difícil de recomendarla.

Making art about colonialism is a fool's errand, a necessary one, but still a fool's errand. The problem being that as a historical phenomenon, once you understand colonialism on a functional level, it’s appalling nature is self-evident. I mean, we quite literally still live in its aftermath, it’s pretty much impossible to go a day without some reminder of its legacy being present in your life. That makes it pretty damn challenging for a piece of art to really serve a constructive or insightful purpose, and Zama is no exception. It’s a very deliberate slog, one with cramped shots, bug-infested soundscapes, and long, monotonous conversations between colonial elites about mind-numbing nothingness. So yeah, it’s a film that practically dares its viewers to tune out, a film that works much better as something to think about with regard to how well-crafted it is, rather than something to watch. I really don’t wanna call it boring, because at the end of the day, it’s fairly well-made, but it’s quite honestly excruciating to watch. I’m far from opposed to a movie having a slow pace, or a deliberately unconventional style, but that can’t be its defining aspect. I watch movies to feel, to think, not be subjected to an artist's self-satisfied conveyor belt of irksome quirks.

pacifiction, l’aura et le fun en moins Je dois reconnaître qu’un certain ennui m’a saisi devant ce film, ennui pourtant travaillé de l’intérieur par une forme d’intérêt. Il s’agit de l’histoire d’un colon espagnol en Argentine à la fin du XVIIIe siècle qui désire revenir en Espagne auprès de sa femme et de ses enfants, mais dont le sort demeure suspendu à l’arbitraire de la monarchie et de ses relais administratifs. Ce récit apparent recouvre en réalité un processus plus profond : la lente désagrégation d’une figure de domination qui découvre, dans le décalage entre sa position imaginaire et sa condition réelle, qu’il n’est rien. Le film travaille alors cette chute non comme un événement spectaculaire mais comme une expérience sensible. Le son notamment se resserre, s’étouffe, jusqu’à laisser place à une sorte de rumeur sourde au moment précis où le personnage perd prise sur le réel et voit s’effondrer les signes de son prestige. La réalisatrice met également en scène les dispositifs de domination. L’homme est pris dans un réseau de rapports qui excèdent sa propre conscience : une épouse l’attend en Espagne, il a engrossé une femme "indigène", il drague l’une des jeunes filles du blanchisseur, il tente en vain de séduire l’épouse d’un représentant de la couronne, laquelle lui échappe précisément parce qu’elle ne se laisse pas assigner à la place qu’il lui destine. Ce faisceau de relations laisse entrevoir une articulation des rapports de domination, à la fois coloniaux et sexués. Aussi le travail du regard participe de ce dispositif. Souvent la scène se dérobe en tant que telle et ce sont les visages de ceux qui regardent qui nous sont donnés, comme si le film déplaçait le centre de gravité de l’action vers ses effets et ses répercussions subjectives. Ce choix produit une forme de décentrement qui redouble la perte de maîtrise du personnage. Enfin, la couleur, avec ces verts persistants et ces oranges poussés jusqu’à une sorte d’intensité terminale dans les dernières séquences, compose une matière visuelle d’une grande beauté comme si l’image elle-même portait, à son niveau, la trace de cette montée vers une limite. Malheureusement, tout cela ne m’a pas suffit pour faire en sorte de ne pas être profondément ennuyé.

Even with the Indios Tabajaras in the background, the movie managed to disappoint me and get me uncomfortable as much as the good baroque artists' enterprise managed to do, breaking the comfortable logic of imperialism. What was exactly what the Spaniards came to do? What is the purpose of the lawyers, the leguleyos, the scribes? So yes, there is this very XXth-century ambition to estrange and attack the logic of the intellectuals coming to confirm something that, in its very bottom, is inconfirmable and relies more on the reconquest for the reconquest for the sole adaption and expansion of syncretism. The traps of the signs, the labyrinths of meaning in a colony that has turned into an absurd place, with not many things to do, not many opportunities, catered towards either the sadism or the hedonism of its peninsular inhabitants. The criollos, as second-order Spaniards in a sense, become disposable populations; there is an outsiderness that comes with existential angst, an out-of-placeness that will be enforced upon the land and the societal. Perhaps more familiar with the US experience of the destruction of any indigeneity or correlation with the ground, the peculiarity here is that the hidalguia and the abstractive nature of the writers will cut that window of release that labor could have brought. When the writer tries to make some fiction, it is forbidden, as in a sense there isn’t even an allowance for the recreation of consciousness or of intelligence. Rather than living, the colonialists are walking symbols, vulnerable to their careerism. The body of the Vicuña Porto means the opportunity to break from the monotonous, to think of the land as something fully captured, fully dominated, and that can be transited. That will be more of the XIXth-century pact, but for the moment any person who wants to dismantle the assuredness of the powers in place will partake in its performativity of otherness. The hands are cut off to remind the loss of agency, the loss of action, the loss of participation in the land, the horrible castaway place of the intellectual. All of this is intriguing and exciting, but I have to subscribe to the critics of Latinamericanism: they are still intellectual feuds, repositioning the intellectual as the main subject of the story, as the most interesting or important piece of the empire, losing a whole broader picture. I get that there is a natural inclination for the writers or scholars to think of Angel Rama's legacy of where to position the empire of the letter beside that of the sword and call for its miseries, but still… it comes off as unnecessary, dull, reiterative, too allegorical, too tryhard. Way too easy to point out the servants as mute figures, the indigenous as second-order existences not captured or grasped by Zama, lived realities which amplify his isolation to reinforce the theme of impotence. Why is the drama always his? Why reinforce the subalternism who cannot speak? The decadence of the promiscuous Spanish woman is already a common trope of the false performativity of the colonial elites, always yearning for somewhere else. As much as the family he cannot access, the alienation of his agency, his lost home—we all feel that despair—but still, aren't we falling into the trap of feeling worse for the criollo than for the others, always reading the colonialism in his own terms? We already knew the illegitimacy of the crown and its absurdity, that has to come with stupid social norms skipped with the necessity for action. Feel sorry for the leguleyos not to be able to listen to the natural rhythm of the Indios Tabajaras?

Zama (2017) es una película de cine nacional dirigida por la siempre interesante Lucrecia Martel. En este caso nos presenta un drama de época sobre un corregidor español en la "Argentina" colonial del Siglo XVIII que atraviesa una travesía de burocracia para lograr su deseo de que lo trasladen de lugar. Primero que nada, hay que destacar la enorme creatividad de Lucrecia Martel para hacer una película tan poco convencional como esta, porque es una película que no se ve todos los días y la directora se mete en el barro para contar esta historia tomándose todo el tiempo del mundo, con una narrativa muy interesante y los recursos que solamente Lucrecia nos puede entregar. En este sentido, la narrativa sería una mezcla entre una pesadilla de David Lynch con una historia de la Argentina Colonial. Pesadilla Lyncheana básicamente porque vamos a ver la historia de este protagonista en relación a su ahogo y frustración con respecto al lugar y la posición que ocupa. Para realizar esta trama, Lucrecia Martel hace un laburo estupendo, en especial con el uso de sonidos, para demostrar la claustrofobia del protagonista, unido a una serie de planos cortos que encierra al protagonista en este lugar que detesta tanto y no consigue salir. La sofocación, los impulsos sexuales, el ambiente húmedo y tenso, todo se responde a partir de los recursos de la cámara y el sonido. En especial, Lucrecia va a utilizar el agua como recurso y vehículo de la tragedia que va sufriendo el protagonista. Así, el agua viene a explicar el "ahogo" de Zama. Sin embargo, el mayor problema que tengo con este film es que me aburrió sobremanera, toda la historia que expliqué anteriormente no logra enganchar en ningún momento, haciendo que no te interese lo que le pase al protagonista ni a ninguno de los personajes que aparece en este film. Si bien en los últimos 10 minutos repunta un montón, haciendo un final más que decente donde podemos ver la calidad que tiene Lucrecia para filmar, no es suficiente para lograr que sea una película recordable. Quizás sea por el guión que hace que la película durante muchos tramos se torne muy pesada y lenta de seguir. Hay películas que son lentas y aun así logran ser una obra maestra, aca pasa poco y nada y no logra conectar con el espectador. También creo que el guión falla con el desarrollo de los personajes, que tampoco transmiten nada, ni para bien ni para mal. Los protagonistas o personajes no logran un sentimiento de empatía (ni siquiera de odio) por parte del espectador. Es como si los mismos personajes fueran los espectadores. En conclusión, Zama está lejos de ser una mala película, ya que se ve lo increíble que es Lucrecia Martel para entregarnos recursos cinematográficos para contar una historia a partir del juego de planos, sonidos y el agua. Sin embargo, mal uso de personajes, de escenas y de momentos, hace que la película se torne densa y, durante gran parte, aburrida. 50 de 100 Gasparcitos.

Making art about colonialism is a fool's errand, a necessary one, but still a fool's errand. The problem being that as a historical phenomenon, once you understand colonialism on a functional level, it’s appalling nature is self-evident. I mean, we quite literally still live in its aftermath, it’s pretty much impossible to go a day without some reminder of its legacy being present in your life. That makes it pretty damn challenging for a piece of art to really serve a constructive or insightful purpose, and Zama is no exception. It’s a very deliberate slog, one with cramped shots, bug-infested soundscapes, and long, monotonous conversations between colonial elites about mind-numbing nothingness. So yeah, it’s a film that practically dares its viewers to tune out, a film that works much better as something to think about with regard to how well-crafted it is, rather than something to watch. I really don’t wanna call it boring, because at the end of the day, it’s fairly well-made, but it’s quite honestly excruciating to watch. I’m far from opposed to a movie having a slow pace, or a deliberately unconventional style, but that can’t be its defining aspect. I watch movies to feel, to think, not be subjected to an artist's self-satisfied conveyor belt of irksome quirks.

pacifiction, l’aura et le fun en moins Je dois reconnaître qu’un certain ennui m’a saisi devant ce film, ennui pourtant travaillé de l’intérieur par une forme d’intérêt. Il s’agit de l’histoire d’un colon espagnol en Argentine à la fin du XVIIIe siècle qui désire revenir en Espagne auprès de sa femme et de ses enfants, mais dont le sort demeure suspendu à l’arbitraire de la monarchie et de ses relais administratifs. Ce récit apparent recouvre en réalité un processus plus profond : la lente désagrégation d’une figure de domination qui découvre, dans le décalage entre sa position imaginaire et sa condition réelle, qu’il n’est rien. Le film travaille alors cette chute non comme un événement spectaculaire mais comme une expérience sensible. Le son notamment se resserre, s’étouffe, jusqu’à laisser place à une sorte de rumeur sourde au moment précis où le personnage perd prise sur le réel et voit s’effondrer les signes de son prestige. La réalisatrice met également en scène les dispositifs de domination. L’homme est pris dans un réseau de rapports qui excèdent sa propre conscience : une épouse l’attend en Espagne, il a engrossé une femme "indigène", il drague l’une des jeunes filles du blanchisseur, il tente en vain de séduire l’épouse d’un représentant de la couronne, laquelle lui échappe précisément parce qu’elle ne se laisse pas assigner à la place qu’il lui destine. Ce faisceau de relations laisse entrevoir une articulation des rapports de domination, à la fois coloniaux et sexués. Aussi le travail du regard participe de ce dispositif. Souvent la scène se dérobe en tant que telle et ce sont les visages de ceux qui regardent qui nous sont donnés, comme si le film déplaçait le centre de gravité de l’action vers ses effets et ses répercussions subjectives. Ce choix produit une forme de décentrement qui redouble la perte de maîtrise du personnage. Enfin, la couleur, avec ces verts persistants et ces oranges poussés jusqu’à une sorte d’intensité terminale dans les dernières séquences, compose une matière visuelle d’une grande beauté comme si l’image elle-même portait, à son niveau, la trace de cette montée vers une limite. Even with the Indios Tabajaras in the background, the movie managed to disappoint me and get me uncomfortable as much as the good baroque artists' enterprise managed to do, breaking the comfortable logic of imperialism. What was exactly what the Spaniards came to do? What is the purpose of the lawyers, the leguleyos, the scribes? So yes, there is this very XXth-century ambition to estrange and attack the logic of the intellectuals coming to confirm something that, in its very bottom, is inconfirmable and relies more on the reconquest for the reconquest for the sole adaption and expansion of syncretism. The traps of the signs, the labyrinths of meaning in a colony that has turned into an absurd place, with not many things to do, not many opportunities, catered towards either the sadism or the hedonism of its peninsular inhabitants. The criollos, as second-order Spaniards in a sense, become disposable populations; there is an outsiderness that comes with existential angst, an out-of-placeness that will be enforced upon the land and the societal. Perhaps more familiar with the US experience of the destruction of any indigeneity or correlation with the ground, the peculiarity here is that the hidalguia and the abstractive nature of the writers will cut that window of release that labor could have brought. When the writer tries to make some fiction, it is forbidden, as in a sense there isn’t even an allowance for the recreation of consciousness or of intelligence. Rather than living, the colonialists are walking symbols, vulnerable to their careerism. The body of the Vicuña Porto means the opportunity to break from the monotonous, to think of the land as something fully captured, fully dominated, and that can be transited. That will be more of the XIXth-century pact, but for the moment any person who wants to dismantle the assuredness of the powers in place will partake in its performativity of otherness. The hands are cut off to remind the loss of agency, the loss of action, the loss of participation in the land, the horrible castaway place of the intellectual. All of this is intriguing and exciting, but I have to subscribe to the critics of Latinamericanism: they are still intellectual feuds, repositioning the intellectual as the main subject of the story, as the most interesting or important piece of the empire, losing a whole broader picture. I get that there is a natural inclination for the writers or scholars to think of Angel Rama's legacy of where to position the empire of the letter beside that of the sword and call for its miseries, but still… it comes off as unnecessary, dull, reiterative, too allegorical, too tryhard. Way too easy to point out the servants as mute figures, the indigenous as second-order existences not captured or grasped by Zama, lived realities which amplify his isolation to reinforce the theme of impotence. Why is the drama always his? Why reinforce the subalternism who cannot speak? The decadence of the promiscuous Spanish woman is already a common trope of the false performativity of the colonial elites, always yearning for somewhere else. As much as the family he cannot access, the alienation of his agency, his lost home—we all feel that despair—but still, aren't we falling into the trap of feeling worse for the criollo than for the others, always reading the colonialism in his own terms? We already knew the illegitimacy of the crown and its absurdity, that has to come with stupid social norms skipped with the necessity for action. Feel sorry for the leguleyos not to be able to listen to the natural rhythm of the Indios Tabajaras?

Zama (2017) es una película de cine nacional dirigida por la siempre interesante Lucrecia Martel. En este caso nos presenta un drama de época sobre un corregidor español en la "Argentina" colonial del Siglo XVIII que atraviesa una travesía de burocracia para lograr su deseo de que lo trasladen de lugar. Primero que nada, hay que destacar la enorme creatividad de Lucrecia Martel para hacer una película tan poco convencional como esta, porque es una película que no se ve todos los días y la directora se mete en el barro para contar esta historia tomándose todo el tiempo del mundo, con una narrativa muy interesante y los recursos que solamente Lucrecia nos puede entregar. En este sentido, la narrativa sería una mezcla entre una pesadilla de David Lynch con una historia de la Argentina Colonial. Pesadilla Lyncheana básicamente porque vamos a ver la historia de este protagonista en relación a su ahogo y frustración con respecto al lugar y la posición que ocupa. Para realizar esta trama, Lucrecia Martel hace un laburo estupendo, en especial con el uso de sonidos, para demostrar la claustrofobia del protagonista, unido a una serie de planos cortos que encierra al protagonista en este lugar que detesta tanto y no consigue salir. La sofocación, los impulsos sexuales, el ambiente húmedo y tenso, todo se responde a partir de los recursos de la cámara y el sonido. En especial, Lucrecia va a utilizar el agua como recurso y vehículo de la tragedia que va sufriendo el protagonista. Así, el agua viene a explicar el "ahogo" de Zama. Sin embargo, el mayor problema que tengo con este film es que me aburrió sobremanera, toda la historia que expliqué anteriormente no logra enganchar en ningún momento, haciendo que no te interese lo que le pase al protagonista ni a ninguno de los personajes que aparece en este film. Si bien en los últimos 10 minutos repunta un montón, haciendo un final más que decente donde podemos ver la calidad que tiene Lucrecia para filmar, no es suficiente para lograr que sea una película recordable. Quizás sea por el guión que hace que la película durante muchos tramos se torne muy pesada y lenta de seguir. Hay películas que son lentas y aun así logran ser una obra maestra, aca pasa poco y nada y no logra conectar con el espectador. También creo que el guión falla con el desarrollo de los personajes, que tampoco transmiten nada, ni para bien ni para mal. Los protagonistas o personajes no logran un sentimiento de empatía (ni siquiera de odio) por parte del espectador. Es como si los mismos personajes fueran los espectadores. En conclusión, Zama está lejos de ser una mala película, ya que se ve lo increíble que es Lucrecia Martel para entregarnos recursos cinematográficos para contar una historia a partir del juego de planos, sonidos y el agua. Sin embargo, mal uso de personajes, de escenas y de momentos, hace que la película se torne densa y, durante gran parte, aburrida. 50 de 100 Gasparcitos.

Me gustaría dejar como conclusión un comentario dejado  por alguien en uno de los tráiler de la película: "no tiene absolutamente nada que decir y aun así se empecina en hacerlo ¡maravilloso!" P.D: O la amas o la odias P.D. 2: No me gusta poner calificaciones numéricas, pero esta película se merece un 2

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "positivas" (3.5–5 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews positivas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):

Lucrecia Martel dirige en un guión excelente sin embargo el ritmo se me hizo denso. Sobre el papel tiene sentido busca trasmitir la sensación de agobio y abandono que siente Don Diego de Zama en una interpretación soberbia de Daniel Giménez Cacho. Es una crítica descarnada al colonianismo que pone en foco lo ridículo y vacío de la burocracia en la conquista, busca desmitificar el como se los percibe generalmente. Ese traslado que no llega y la vida en Sudamérica desgasta a Don Diego física y mentalmente en un tercer acto certero y casi surrealista donde la fotografía y el sonido que transporta son un lujo.

[8] nota=3.5 estrelas:
Espera de largo aliento en la ribera fronteriza Paraguay-Argentina, donde el aburrimiento, la enfermedad y el calor componen el patético retrato del funcionario Diego de Zama, cuyo destino pende de la Corona española. Cambio de época y género, Martel reincide en la decadencia de la clase dominante aprovechando el contexto colonial, marcando la distancia espacial mas no moral entre indio y español. Así, esos valores puros y burgueses se rinden ante el instinto animal, violento y carnal, detrimento ajeno a la normalidad del pueblo dominado, quienes se entregan al claroscuro humano sin aparentar grandeza. La realización es la igualdad de condiciones mortales lejos del poder, poder que el propio Zama no posee en su totalidad. Como muñeca rusa, es la historia de gente dominada que domina, cuyo status es intrascendente al campo abierto de la tradición cultural originaria o el mal mutable sin nombre propio. Vicuña, criminal, bestia, la peste moral del violador y asesino Diego de Zama.

Zama oozes orientalism out of its pores with exotic music that has an ironic side effect. Suggesting a tropical paradise that in fact is a hellhole from which everyone wants to escape, only Zama doesn’t have this luck. It’s a story that spans over an unknown amount of time yet we see Zama getting older, especially near the end when he has grown a beard and needs to hunt down a ferocious outlaw so he can be transferred to another place. However luck isn’t on his side as he probably will always remain trapped in the jungle most people would define as an tropic and luxury vacation destination. Zama is the story of a failed character, one that doesn’t seem able enough to escape his destiny and grows more paranoid the days go by with the excellent suggestive sounddesign. Zama is the obvious critique on colonialism and makes it very clear in the way it shows the highest of high degrade to the level of the lowest and possibly even lower. In other words: a man without any agency, only dependent on others.

“I do for you what nobody did for me. I say no to your hopes.” “Shove your stumps in the sand. If you don’t bleed out, you’ll survive.” My first Martel. I like movies that put you in the same epistemic position as their main character, and the audience is meant to feel as disoriented and adrift as Zama does. There are moments where I had less faith that Martel was steering the adrift-ness, but once I realized this was the type of film where you have to fully give yourself over to the viewing experience I started having a good time. I trust that dissatisfaction and confusion were the emotions Martel intended me to feel, and she certainly succeeded (and I mean that as praise)! Really amazing framing and blocking. Super visually claustrophobic. So many crowded frames that blocked my sightline. Her sound design was great and really unnerving; the sound kept arriving from off-screen, from spaces I couldn't see, so I was always slightly behind the film. The sets and costuming and location were incredible, and I'm now so curious as to what was historically ~accurate~, what was anachronistic, and what was purely invented. Might be an interesting double feature with Beau Travail.

His loneliness is atrocious. Lucrecia Martel’s films have such excellent sound design. Sounds of nature permeate almost every scene, and I really like how the dialogue dies out when we hear Diego’s inner thoughts. I love how this film depicts colonialism. An elderly couple complains that they have no one to work on their land because they’ve killed all the Indians in the area. Slaves are in the background of several scenes, and their masters are casually cruel, if they pay their slaves any attention at all. These Spaniards seek to conquer and kill and have no regard for the indigenous people’s way of life. The plot feels a little aimless, but to me that enhances the narrative. Auto translation by AI. (Original: Japanese) My first Lucrecia Martel film. An Argentine female director. I wanted to see her other two films being screened, but this was the only one that fit my schedule (Tokyo FILMeX). Set in the late 18th century on the frontier of Latin America, a Spanish colony. The protagonist, Don Diego de Zama, a local colonial administrator, is a Criollo (a "white" person born in colonial Latin America, not in Spain itself), and the fact that he harbors a conflicted ("white") consciousness about this is likely important to the story's premise. Unlike whites born in Spain, it seems there is a ceiling to how high a Criollo can be promoted. From the very beginning, Zama is easily stripped of his "dignity." He peeks at indigenous women bathing in the mud, is scolded and chased away, but reveals his weakness by slapping one of the women in return. He also desires Luciana, a noblewoman who came from Spain (which is the same as desiring the center of the empire), and tries to take advantage of her, but is rejected. He makes passes at a mixed-race local woman who came to petition him (one can read sexual violence by white men in the background), but is treated coldly, and so on. Even if a return to Spain is impossible, he hopes for a transfer to a slightly more prestigious colonial city and submits a petition to the King of Spain, but a reply from the center of the empire never arrives, and it continues to be postponed for no reason (this absurdity and the emptiness and futility of the bureaucracy are reminiscent of Kafka's world). He keeps waiting, but he cannot obtain anything. At the beginning, an indigenous prisoner told a fable about a fish and water. One fish spends its whole life swimming; the water tries to throw the fish onto land, and the fish resists. Even though the water rejects the fish, the fish clings to the water forever, using up all its strength just to stay there. They are always on the shore, not in the middle of the river, he said... Since the screen immediately captures Zama's back as he stands on the shore after this, it is clear that this is a metaphor for Zama's situation. In this region, a villain named Vicuña Porto is running rampant, and public order is deteriorating. According to rumors, some say Vicuña is dead, others say they killed him, so the truth is unknown. Zama joins a group to hunt down Vicuña (to make a name for himself)... Who exactly is Vicuña Porto? Is he one person? Or is he an omnipresent, invisible "Other"? In the end, with both hands severed and literally unable to hold anything, Zama is placed on a small boat rowed by an indigenous boy and drifts slowly through a wetland area where green algae and moss cover the water's surface like a membrane. The boy asks, "Do you want to live?" The power of life and death is now in the hands of the indigenous boy. Zama nods slightly. And the story closes with the gentle, tropical sound of an acoustic guitar that feels out of place... What a fable. It is an ending that could be considered ambiguous; perhaps... at the end of this journey, has Zama finally found "harmony" with this environment that he has been rejecting all along? (November 28, 2025, Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho)

Zama (2017) follows the life of Don Diego de Zama, a Spanish official with little power who yearns for a transfer to a more prestigious post back home. The film is a slow burning existential crisis as Zama descends in status in the colony. The film considers themes such as power, colonialism, class, ethnicity and gender. Zama is marked by his otherness from all other characters in the film. This begins when he is caught voyeuring on some local women bathing. They chase him away, upset with his existence in their environment. This is continued when he is not fully respected by the men he works with. Despite being white, he is seen as lesser than because he was not born in Europe. It is revealed in his interactions with Luciania that despite her being a woman her status supersedes his because of her class and Spanish ethnicity. The film plays with fascinating power dynamics between class, race, and gender. Director Lucrecia Martel uses nudity to underscore the lower status of the native women and to reveal their role as objects of primal desire for the white colonizers. I highly recommend looking into the historical context surrounding this movie before watching, so that you can appreciate the film without struggling to understand what is happening. When I watched, it was hard for me to appreciate the film as much as I could have, because I was busy trying to understand the context. This seems to be a film that grows in its appeal on its second watch. It is complex, slow moving, and yet director Lucrecia Martel leaves much for the audience to ruminate over.

Auto translation by AI. (Original: Japanese) My first Lucrecia Martel film. An Argentine female director. I wanted to see her other two films being screened, but this was the only one that fit my schedule (Tokyo FILMeX). Set in the late 18th century on the frontier of Latin America, a Spanish colony. The protagonist, Don Diego de Zama, a local colonial administrator, is a Criollo (a "white" person born in colonial Latin America, not in Spain itself), and the fact that he harbors a conflicted ("white") consciousness about this is likely important to the story's premise. Unlike whites born in Spain, it seems there is a ceiling to how high a Criollo can be promoted. From the very beginning, Zama is easily stripped of his "dignity." He peeks at indigenous women bathing in the mud, is scolded and chased away, but reveals his weakness by slapping one of the women in return. He also desires Luciana, a noblewoman who came from Spain (which is the same as desiring the center of the empire), and tries to take advantage of her, but is rejected. He makes passes at a mixed-race local woman who came to petition him (one can read sexual violence by white men in the background), but is treated coldly, and so on. Even if a return to Spain is impossible, he hopes for a transfer to a slightly more prestigious colonial city and submits a petition to the King of Spain, but a reply from the center of the empire never arrives, and it continues to be postponed for no reason (this absurdity and the emptiness and futility of the bureaucracy are reminiscent of Kafka's world). He keeps waiting, but he cannot obtain anything. At the beginning, an indigenous prisoner told a fable about a fish and water. One fish spends its whole life swimming; the water tries to throw the fish onto land, and the fish resists. Even though the water rejects the fish, the fish clings to the water forever, using up all its strength just to stay there. They are always on the shore, not in the middle of the river, he said... Since the screen immediately captures Zama's back as he stands on the shore after this, it is clear that this is a metaphor for Zama's situation. In this region, a villain named Vicuña Porto is running rampant, and public order is deteriorating. According to rumors, some say Vicuña is dead, others say they killed him, so the truth is unknown. Zama joins a group to hunt down Vicuña (to make a name for himself)... Who exactly is Vicuña Porto? Is he one person? Or is he an omnipresent, invisible "Other"? In the end, with both hands severed and literally unable to hold anything, Zama is placed on a small boat rowed by an indigenous boy and drifts slowly through a wetland area where green algae and moss cover the water's surface like a membrane. The boy asks, "Do you want to live?" The power of life and death is now in the hands of the indigenous boy. Zama nods slightly. And the story closes with the gentle, tropical sound of an acoustic guitar that feels out of place... What a fable. It is an ending that could be considered ambiguous; perhaps... at the end of this journey, has Zama finally found "harmony" with this environment that he has been rejecting all along? (November 28, 2025, Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho)

Zama (2017) follows the life of Don Diego de Zama, a Spanish official with little power who yearns for a transfer to a more prestigious post back home. The film is a slow burning existential crisis as Zama descends in status in the colony. The film considers themes such as power, colonialism, class, ethnicity and gender. Zama is marked by his otherness from all other characters in the film. This begins when he is caught voyeuring on some local women bathing. They chase him away, upset with his existence in their environment. This is continued when he is not fully respected by the men he works with. Despite being white, he is seen as lesser than because he was not born in Europe. It is revealed in his interactions with Luciania that despite her being a woman her status supersedes his because of her class and Spanish ethnicity. The film plays with fascinating power dynamics between class, race, and gender. Director Lucrecia Martel uses nudity to underscore the lower status of the native women and to reveal their role as objects of primal desire for the white colonizers. I highly recommend looking into the historical context surrounding this movie before watching, so that you can appreciate the film without struggling to understand what is happening. When I watched, it was hard for me to appreciate the film as much as I could have, because I was busy trying to understand the context. This seems to be a film that grows in its appeal on its second watch. It is complex, slow moving, and yet director Lucrecia Martel leaves much for the audience to ruminate over.

Stunning. Tonally precise and so magnificently odd. Traces of Martel's other work set in contemporary times are visible. But the period piece elements here are put to fantastic use. A dissection of colonial absurdity, abuse, and failure. After the first few shots it felt claustrophobic for much of the first half, with few exterior shots and lots of interior sets. This seems to change towards the end, when it opens up more towards exteriors. I need to rewatch this on a big screen when I am more awake, as I was nodding off at home watching this after a long day. It might be a masterpiece.

[37] nota=5.0 estrelas:
Don Diego de Zama (Daniel Giménez Cacho), representante de la Corona española en América que recibe el burlesco apelativo de "Corregidor", es un hombre tan minúsculo en su moralidad que sus ridículas pretensiones (ser promovido para irse del lugar al que fue enviado) hablan de su negación desesperada por demostrar lo opuesto. Prefiere endilgarle epítetos a aquellos que critican a su interés amoroso Luciana Piñares de Luenga (Lola Dueñas) antes de asumir que él representa una porción de ese sistema colonial que aquí hemos visto esclavizando y sometiendo a la población autóctona. Por eso, tanto pueblos originarios como los blancos que lo acompañaban en esa expedición eligen a Zama para sacárselo de encima... Con una inteligencia que abarca crítica social dura, humor sutil, prolijidad visual y sonora en cucharadas justas, Lucrecia Martel nos lleva a un tiempo clave de la historia continental para que recordemos de dónde venimos sin privarnos de ver las aristas más dolorosas. La estupidez y la maldad ya definían a los poderosos hace tres siglos. Ojalá que algún día eso se termine. NOTA: cinco estrellas!

"No puedo saber como serán mis hijos, pero si sé como será este libro." La opus magnum de Martel. Todo lo que caracteriza su cine (los cuerpos incomodos, el tiempo absurdo y angustioso, la naturaleza) se adapta y funciona perfectamente en la época colonial. Porque si los sistemas son absurdos, ¿quien dice que no fueron así desde su concepción?. Ver a Don Diego de Zama intentar algo tan simple como irse y acabar como acaba tiene un aire inevitable. Como si un solo papel de renuncia fuera tu sentencia de muerte. No servís si te quejas.
